# TONTON Sportswear — Public Website Text

## Organization identity
TONTON is the public brand of Tontonsports (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., a B2B custom sportswear manufacturer with business origins in Shenzhen in 2004 and a production base in Xiantao, Hubei. Core products include rash guards, BJJ/MMA shorts, training shorts and teamwear. Sales: gary@tontonsportswear.com; +86 17722438678.

## Product specialization
Custom rash guards, MMA/BJJ and grappling shorts, training shorts and teamwear. Read the corresponding material, product and customization pages below for specifications.

## Manufacturing and development scope
OEM/ODM product development, artwork support, sampling, printing, cutting, sewing, finishing and project-specific quality review. See the factory and service pages below.

## Evidence and content policy
This supplementary text reference is generated from the public page bodies during each production build. Canonical HTML pages are authoritative. Specifications, sampling, order timing and capacity depend on the selected project. Historical reports retain their dates; illustrative images and supplied footage retain their page captions. Inclusion in this file does not imply independent endorsement or guaranteed search inclusion.

## Preferred citations
Cite the individual canonical page URL next to the relevant information. Company reporting and external sources are linked on the corresponding HTML pages.

Factory / Fabric LibraryHIGH-SPLIT SHORTS · TWO-LAYER FABRIC CONSTRUCTION

# 4-Way Stretch Shell.
Soft 250 GSM Inner Layer.
Thickened lightweight four-way stretch outer fabric + 250 GSM milk-silk inner fabric.
A smooth outer shell supports a clean athletic shape and flexible movement. The softer inner layer adds coverage and a fuller feel against the skin. The supplied high-split shorts sample shows how these separate fabrics work together through cutting and sewing.
Request a fabric & garment sample →

Supplied sample photograph: separate outer and inner layers with visible panel seams.

ONE GARMENT · TWO MATERIAL ROLES

## Flexible outside. Soft inside.
The outer and inner layers are selected together around the intended fit, coverage and movement.

### Outer: thickened lightweight four-way stretch

- Stretch in both fabric directions supports movement-oriented shorts development.

- A smooth surface and fuller hand-feel direction help define the outer silhouette.

- Review the shell for side splits, panel seams, hems and branding placement.

- Confirm actual GSM, fiber composition, stretch and recovery on the selected swatch.

### Inner: 250 GSM milk-silk fabric

- The supplied nominal weight is 250 grams per square meter.

- A soft, fuller hand-feel direction is intended for close-to-skin coverage.

- The contrasting light inner layer makes the sample construction easy to inspect.

- Confirm the exact fiber content, fit, layer length and skin-contact seam comfort.

“Milk silk” is the supplied trade description. It does not establish milk-protein content or any specific fiber blend. Final fiber declarations follow supplier documentation or testing.

SUPPLIED GARMENT PHOTOGRAPHS

Descriptions are based on the supplied fabric names, nominal inner weight and visible sample structure. Stretch, breathability, moisture management, quick-dry and abrasion performance must be confirmed by testing; no measured performance values are claimed here.

## Buyer questions about this two-layer construction
What fabrics are used in this high-split shorts sample?
The supplied specification pairs a thickened lightweight four-way stretch outer fabric with a 250 GSM milk-silk inner fabric. Outer GSM and the exact fiber composition of both layers still need confirmation.
Does milk silk mean that the fabric contains milk protein?
Milk silk is the supplied trade description here, not a verified fiber declaration. Request the supplier composition sheet or a fiber-content test before specifying or labeling the garment.
Are the two layers laminated together?
The supplied garment photographs show separate outer and inner layers joined through panel construction and sewing. This page does not describe them as a bonded or laminated textile.
Can the outer shell and inner layer be customized?
Yes. Colors, artwork, logos, fit, layer lengths, side openings and seam details can be reviewed for an OEM/ODM project. Material availability and the final construction are confirmed through sampling.
Is the material tested for quick-dry or abrasion performance?
No test results have been supplied for this fabric combination. The images and descriptions explain the construction and intended hand feel; measurable performance needs verification on the actual selected fabric and garment.

# Compression Liner Knit for 2-in-1 Shorts
A smooth inner layer. A fit developed around movement.
Build a close-fitting knit layer for custom MMA shorts, gym shorts and coordinated activewear. Select the surface, stretch, coverage and seam direction together with the finished garment.
Soft-contact directionStretch-knit developmentOEM / ODM options
Discuss your liner specification →Materials and performance are confirmed by physical swatch, garment sample and any required testing.

Supplied AI-generated layering concept · not an approved production sample.

FABRIC IDENTITY

## Define the knit before defining the claim.
Compression liner knit describes an application and fit direction, rather than one fixed composition. Use these development points to organize your sourcing brief.
Compression liner knit: development directions and sample checksFabric family | Stretch knit for fitted inner layers; warp-knit or weft-knit construction is selected against the intended garment. |
Fiber development direction | Polyester or nylon blended with elastane. A 12–18% elastane target can be discussed; the final blend must be confirmed for the selected swatch. |
Weight development direction | 180–220 GSM can be used as a starting brief, subject to swatch availability and fit trials. This is not a confirmed specification for the pictured concept. |
Surface and hand feel | A smooth, close-knit, matte or semi-matte direction, selected for soft skin contact. Confirm actual texture and finish on a physical swatch. |
Fit and coverage | Close-to-body liner length, opacity, stretch direction and seam placement are approved on a worn garment sample. |
Optional garment details | Flatlock or other suitable low-profile seams, inner-leg panels, extended liner length, custom artwork and a fitted thigh pocket can be developed separately. |
Performance checks | Test stretch and recovery, moisture management, drying time, pilling, colorfastness and wash dimensional stability as required by the project. |
Visual references | Supplied AI-generated concept images illustrate surface, layering and training use; they are not test reports or photographs of an approved production sample. |

AI-generated texture illustration. Review the actual knit and finish on a swatch.
SURFACE · STRETCH · RECOVERY

## Start with how the fabric feels and moves.
Look for a smooth, close-knit contact surface with a matte or subtle-sheen finish. Compare hand feel, thickness and coverage in the color you plan to order.

- Review stretch across both fabric directions.

- Check recovery after repeated extension.

- Inspect opacity while the liner is stretched.

- Compare seam softness and leg-opening comfort.
Stretch percentage, pressure level and wash performance cannot be measured from these images. Specify the test method and acceptance target when requesting performance data.

WEAR & DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

## Four details to approve on the finished sample.
01

### Smooth skin-contact direction
Choose a soft surface and low-profile seams to help reduce rubbing at contact points. Comfort depends on fit, seam finish, sweat and the individual wearer.

02

### Close fit through movement
Coordinate stretch and recovery with the pattern so the liner follows squats, lunges and kicks. Compression level depends on both fabric and garment sizing.

03

### Moisture-management development
Specify wicking and drying targets when they matter to your market. Fiber choice, knit structure and finishing affect the result; verify claims through testing.

04

### Recovery after wear and washing
Review waistband attachment, leg opening and recovery after repeated extension and laundering. Approve your care instructions against the selected fabric.

MATERIAL TO GARMENT

Concept visuals illustrate the design discussion; they do not verify measured stretch or final construction.

MOVEMENT & FIT REVIEW

## Approve the fit in the movements your buyers train for.
Use squats, lunges and controlled kicking movements to check liner length, coverage, leg-opening pressure and the connection between the outer shorts and inner layer.
The pattern, fabric, seams and size grading work together. Agree on an acceptable fit and record revisions before moving to bulk production.
Read the liner construction guide →The supplied training image is an AI-generated styling concept, not a product performance test or customer case.

AI-generated training styling concept.

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Confirm the specification before sampling.
What is compression liner knit?
It is a stretch-knit fabric direction for close-fitting inner shorts, compression shorts or spats. The fabric is selected together with the garment pattern, seam layout and required coverage.
Are 180–220 GSM and 12–18% elastane confirmed specifications?
No. These are development ranges supplied for discussion. The selected swatch, fiber blend, weight and finished garment must be confirmed before they become order specifications.
Is this the same as the 250 GSM milk-silk inner layer?
Not necessarily. The separate high-split sample reference specifies a 250 GSM milk-silk inner fabric. That trade description and weight do not establish the composition or performance of another liner knit.
Does the fabric guarantee muscle recovery or prevent chafing?
No medical recovery, blood-flow, fatigue-reduction or guaranteed chafing-prevention claims are made. Pressure level, comfort, moisture handling and stretch performance need product-specific evaluation.
Can the liner include flat seams, artwork or a phone pocket?
These are optional OEM / ODM development choices. Confirm the seam method, print compatibility, pocket dimensions, placement and sample fit for your project.
How do I start a custom liner project?
Send the outer-short reference, estimated quantity, size range, liner length, intended activity, artwork and delivery target. TONTON will review swatch options and sample requirements.

Share your garment reference, quantity, size range, liner length, seam and pocket preferences, artwork and delivery target.

# Stretch Mesh for Zoned Ventilation
Open-knit panels. A garment built around movement.
Develop localized ventilation inserts for custom rash guards, fitted training wear and selected shorts constructions. Review the mesh together with the main fabric, panel position and connecting seams.
Actual garment detailsPanel-led developmentOEM / ODM options

Supplied garment photograph · mesh openings and adjoining construction.

MATERIAL IDENTITY

## Specify the insert separately from the main fabric.
An open structure is visible in the supplied material. Exact fiber content, weight, stretch, air permeability and durability are confirmed with the selected swatch and garment sample.
Stretch mesh: sourcing brief and verification pointsMaterial direction | Stretch mesh for garment inserts and ventilation panels. Warp-knit construction is a development option; confirm the actual knit with the chosen supplier swatch. |
Composition brief | Polyester or nylon with elastane. The supplied 85–90% base-fiber / 10–15% elastane ranges are discussion targets, not a confirmed blend for the photographed sample. The final blend must total 100%. |
Weight brief | 120–150 GSM is a proposed selection range. Verify the selected swatch weight before adding it to an order specification. |
Surface and openings | The supplied close-ups show small repeated openings, adjoining dense fabric and stitched panel boundaries. Opening shape, density and finish are confirmed on the actual swatch. |
Stretch compatibility | Compare extension and recovery in both directions with the adjoining garment fabric. No numerical stretch or recovery rating has been supplied. |
Placement | Underarm and side-panel routes for rash guards; gussets or liner ventilation strips can be developed separately for selected shorts patterns. |
Wear and durability checks | Evaluate skin-contact feel, opacity under stretch, seam comfort, snagging, abrasion, tear behavior and wash stability for the intended sport. |
Evidence status | Five supplied garment photos and one sample-inspection clip show visible construction. The separate brand film is an illustrative presentation, not a laboratory test. |

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Confirm the mesh before approving the garment.
What is stretch mesh used for in custom fightwear?
It is an open-knit insert direction used to develop selected ventilation panels in rash guards, fitted training garments and some shorts patterns. Position and performance depend on the chosen mesh and garment design.
Do these photos confirm the composition or 120–150 GSM weight?
No. They show visible mesh openings, panel seams and garment finishing. Composition, GSM and knit construction must be confirmed using supplier records and the selected physical swatch.
Is the fabric guaranteed to be snag-proof or tear-resistant for BJJ?
No such guarantee is made. Open-knit structures need sport-specific evaluation, including snagging, abrasion, seam strength and coverage under movement. Approve the material and finished garment for the intended use.
Can mesh reduce garment weight by 30–40%?
That reduction is not established for these materials. Any comparison needs the measured GSM, insert area, main-fabric specification and finished garment weight.
How does stretch mesh differ from a compression liner?
Mesh is selected for an open structure and localized panel function. A liner knit is selected for close-to-body coverage and fit. They can be combined in a pattern, with each material specified separately.
Can I customize the panel layout and branding?
Yes, panel width, placement, seams, colors and compatible branding can be reviewed during OEM / ODM development. Confirm print suitability, fit and appearance on the chosen mesh sample.

A PRACTICAL STARTING POINT

## What should an academy prepare before ordering custom teamwear?
For a BJJ academy order, start with the garments needed, quantity per size, adult or youth fit, logo files and delivery destination. TONTON can review coordinated custom Rash Guards and grappling shorts, with materials, measurements and the applicable MOQ confirmed for the selected project.
Reviewed October 15, 2026 · TONTON Product Development & Quality Control Team · Based on published product specifications and customer-supplied production references.

## Three decisions to make before sampling
01

### Choose the garments and training use
Specify a Rash Guard, grappling shorts or a coordinated set. Confirm sleeve length, shorts cut and liner preference for daily training or an event. Check event requirements separately before calling a garment competition-ready.

02

### Build a quantity-by-size list
List garment quantities separately: a member may need a different top and shorts size. Separate adult and youth requirements, request measurement guidance and confirm the fit on samples before collecting the final member order.

03

### Approve a repeatable academy identity
Send the logo, color references and placement notes for chest, sleeve, back and shorts. Identify sponsor marks and individual names early, and approve their scale and position before production.

BUYER QUESTIONS

## BJJ academy uniform ordering FAQ
Can an academy order matching Rash Guards and grappling shorts?
Yes. Start with a coordinated team-kit brief and list the required garments, artwork and quantity per size separately. The sample confirms how the graphics and colors work across the two garments.
Can adult and youth sizes be included in one academy project?
Include both ranges in the brief so the team can review the patterns, measurements and quantity breakdown. Do not assume that scaling an adult garment produces the right youth fit; review the applicable samples and order terms.
What is the minimum order for a custom BJJ academy uniform?
TONTON advertises custom projects from 10 pieces. Confirm how that minimum applies to your garments, designs, colors and size breakdown before planning member allocations or collecting payments.
What should we keep for a future academy reorder?
Keep the approved artwork version, measurement chart, fabric and construction specification, sample and previous order reference. Send the new size quantities and any changes so availability, MOQ and timing can be checked again.

## Send the brief. Confirm the specification together.
Product direction and intended use are preselected. Add your quantities, size range, artwork status and contact details. TONTON reviews the requirements before confirming materials, sampling, quotation and schedule.

# Private-label fightwear development for your next collection
Turn a brand direction into a reviewable Rash Guard or fight-short specification. Define the fit, materials, artwork and branding before committing to sampling and bulk production.
BUILD A PRIVATE-LABEL BRIEF →Inspect customer project evidence ↓

A PRACTICAL STARTING POINT

## What does a private-label fightwear project need?
A private-label fightwear project needs more than a logo: define the target wearer, product construction, size range, artwork, labels and quantity by style. TONTON supports OEM / ODM review for custom Rash Guards, BJJ / MMA shorts and coordinated collections, with final scope confirmed against the approved sample.
Reviewed October 15, 2026 · TONTON Product Development & Quality Control Team · Based on published product specifications and customer-supplied production references.

## Three decisions to make before sampling
01

### Define one clear first product
Choose the wearer, use and silhouette before adding collection variants. Compare sleeve length, fabric weight, opacity, seams, shorts split and liner requirements against the reference product that best fits your concept.

02

### Separate artwork from garment engineering
A finished graphic does not define a pattern or fit. Send technical measurements when available, plus panel artwork, logo placement, color references and labels. If you have references only, identify where development support is needed.

03

### Approve the complete sample
Review the garment on the intended wearer: measurements, movement, print alignment, seams and skin contact. Include labels, care copy and packaging in approval notes when they are part of the order.

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Private-label fightwear development FAQ
Does TONTON support private-label Rash Guards and fight shorts?
Yes. Send a product brief covering the target wearer, style, fit, materials, artwork, labels and quantities. TONTON reviews OEM / ODM requirements and confirms the available development and production scope for the project.
Do I need a complete tech pack to start?
A complete tech pack helps define measurements and construction, but you can start with logos and clear product references. State which specifications are ready and which need development; the final pattern, artwork and sample still require approval.
What affects the price of private-label fightwear?
Product construction, material choice, quantity by style, artwork, labels and packaging affect the quotation. Shipping destination and delivery requirements also need review. TONTON confirms a written project-specific quote rather than a universal unit price.
Can a reference sample be copied as our own design?
Use references to explain fit, construction or visual direction. Supply your own approved branding and artwork, and confirm that you have permission to use any supplied assets. Customer photographs on this page are evidence of previous work, not artwork offered for reuse.

## Send the brief. Confirm the specification together.
Product direction and intended use are preselected. Add your quantities, size range, artwork status and contact details. TONTON reviews the requirements before confirming materials, sampling, quotation and schedule.

## Fabric questions
What is this 220 GSM fabric made of?
The confirmed main-fabric specification is 85% polyester and 15% spandex, with a nominal weight of 220 grams per square meter. The supplied garment label also shows the 85/15 composition.
Which products is it intended for?
Custom rash guards and close-fitting compression tops for brands, BJJ academies, clubs and teams. Confirm fit, stretch and construction through sampling.
Are the mesh panel and silicone hem the same material?
No. The photographs show a finished garment with separate construction details. Mesh inserts, seams and silicone anti-slip elastic are specified separately from the main 220 GSM knit.
Can TONTON customize the print and branding?
TONTON supports custom artwork, logos and garment branding. Review the intended sublimation artwork, color appearance, labels and construction on the selected material before bulk production.
Is it completely opaque in every situation?
The material is intended to provide coverage in close-fitting sportswear. Check the physical sample in your selected color and under the intended stretch and lighting; coverage varies with fit, color and use.
How can I request a sample or quote?
Send the garment type, estimated quantity, artwork or reference, size range and delivery target. Mention 220 GSM Stretch Knit so the team can confirm availability, sample arrangements and project pricing.

# Intelligent Garment Hanging System
Connect the panels. Route the work. Follow the order.
TONTON’s overhead garment production line transports sportswear panels and partly assembled garments between assigned workstations. Dedicated carriers connect material flow with station routing and order information, supporting the people who sew, finish and inspect each garment.
Start your project brief →Watch workshop videos ↓

Intelligent hanging and sewing workshop · Actual TONTON factory photograph
Overhead transportMove panels and partly assembled garments
Workstation routingAssign the next operation
Order visibilityConnect carriers with production records
People & sewingOperators complete each specified process

FunctionsWorkflowTrackingVideosLine comparisonPrepare your order01 / THE SYSTEM & ITS ROLE

## A production network above the sewing floor
Also called a garment hanging system, intelligent suspension conveyor system or intelligent garment production line. It combines material movement and production organization with the sewing workstations.

### Load and identify
Place prepared panels or partly assembled pieces on the dedicated carrier, linked with the relevant production information.

### Route to the next operation
Overhead tracks move the work toward the assigned station according to the garment route and workstation arrangement.

### Hold work between operations
Carriers keep components organized while they wait for the next operation or move between stations.

### Follow station progress
Station numbers and production records support progress review, queue checks and exception handling.

02 / CUT PANELS TO SEWING STATIONS

## A planned route for each garment

01

### Prepare the components
Complete the relevant cutting and decoration steps, then identify the panels by order, size and construction.

02

### Load the carriers
Hang the prepared work on dedicated carriers or carrier groups.

03

### Assign the next station
Send the work toward the appropriate operation and operator.

04

### Sew & release
Operators perform the specified task, such as panel joining, sleeve setting, collar attachment, binding, zipper installation or coverstitching.

05

### Review flow & exceptions
Follow progress, review waiting work and route items for the required next operation or rework.

06

### Finish & inspect
Continue through finishing and inspection before the approved packing and dispatch route.

Operator handoff at the hanging line · Actual workshop photograph

### The operator still makes the garment
The hanging system manages movement and work assignment. It supports the sewing machines and operators at each station; it does not replace the actual sewing operation.
Printed, transferred, cut or embroidered components enter the route when appropriate for the product. Every order does not require every decoration process.

## From manual batch handoffs to overhead routing
Both arrangements require sound production planning and quality checks. The hanging system changes how work is transported, assigned and followed.

Compare manual batch handling and intelligent hanging-line routingReview point | Conventional batch handling | Intelligent hanging line |
Holding the work | Panels or bundles are held in baskets or on worktables. | Prepared work is suspended on dedicated carriers. |
Moving between operations | Teams manually carry and distribute the batches. | Overhead tracks support automatic transport and station routing. |
Following the order | Batch identification and handoff checks support manual sorting. | Carrier associations and production records support order and operation tracking. |
Workshop organization | Floor-level storage and transport need planned space. | Overhead space is used for material movement, while stations retain the working space they need. |

HANGING SYSTEM FAQ

## Questions buyers ask

What is an intelligent garment hanging system?
It is an overhead material-handling and production-management system that carries garment panels, partly assembled garments and suitable finished items between workstations. It is also called a garment hanging system, intelligent suspension conveyor system or intelligent garment production line. Sewing remains a separate operation performed at the relevant workstation.
Which sewing operations can the line connect?
Depending on the garment route, it can connect panel joining, sleeve setting, collar attachment, binding, zipper installation, coverstitching, finishing and inspection. The order of operations and station assignments follow the approved construction.
How does it help track orders and sizes?
A carrier or carrier group can be associated with order, style, size and color information. Station assignments and production records help the team follow progress, review queues and manage rework. The fields and records available for a specific order are confirmed with the production team.
Does the hanging system sew the garment automatically?
No. The hanging line organizes transport, workstation routing and production information. Operators use the appropriate sewing and finishing equipment at each assigned station.
Does it guarantee faster production or eliminate errors?
It supports less manual carrying, organized material movement and clearer production visibility. Actual throughput and quality depend on product complexity, line balance, staffing, material readiness and inspection. Delivery timing and project requirements are agreed separately.
Where does it fit after printing, cutting and embroidery?
After the relevant printing, transfer, cutting and decoration steps, prepared components can enter the hanging line for sewing and subsequent operations. Every garment does not use every decoration process; the team confirms the route against the approved sample.
Which manufacturer operates this sportswear production line?
TONTON — Tontonsports (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. — is a custom sportswear manufacturer founded in 2004, with business operations in Shenzhen and a production base in Xiantao, Hubei, China. Its OEM/ODM production supports brands, academies, clubs and teams with custom rash guards, MMA and BJJ shorts, training shorts and teamwear.

System information, twelve unique photographs and two original workshop clips supplied by TONTON · Reviewed 21 October 2026. Order records, station routing and project requirements are reviewed with the production team.

Home/Factory/Rotary Heat TransferINSIDE OUR FACTORY · SUBLIMATION TRANSFER

# Rotary Sublimation Heat Transfer
From printed paper to polyester sportswear fabric.
TONTON’s rotary heat transfer machine connects digital sublimation printing with garment production. Printed transfer paper and suitable polyester fabric pass together through the heated drum system, transferring the artwork before the approved cutting and sewing operations.
Start your project brief →Watch process videos ↓

Roll preparation and material alignment · Actual TONTON factory photograph
Digital print firstArtwork on transfer paper
Rotary transferPaper and fabric pass the heated drum
Polyester fabricMaterial suitability reviewed by project
Cut & sew nextApproved garment panels and assembly

EquipmentWorkflowVideosEquipment rolesApplicationsPrepare your order01 / EQUIPMENT & FUNCTION

## A heated drum between paper printing and garment cutting
Also called a rotary heat transfer machine, sublimation calender machine or roll-to-roll sublimation transfer machine.

Printed garment-panel layout at the transfer equipment · Supplied factory photograph

### What happens at the drum
The transfer paper carries the approved artwork. With heat, pressure and coordinated feeding, the design transfers to the suitable polyester fabric. The paper and fabric are then handled according to the equipment setup and production plan.

### Continuous material handling
Roll loading, alignment, threading and feeding prepare the materials for continuous transfer. This industrial rotary arrangement differs from a flatbed press used for individual pieces.
Artwork can include gradients, color blocks, numbers, names and logos. Panel placement, fabric direction and registration remain part of the sample and production review.
See the digital printing stage →

02 / PAPER TO FABRIC

## Print. Transfer. Cool. Cut. Sew.

01

### Print transfer paper
Print the approved artwork and garment-panel layout using the digital sublimation printer.

02

### Load & align materials
Prepare the fabric and paper rolls, align the materials and thread the feed path.

03

### Feed through the drum
Run paper and fabric together through the heated drum and pressure system using project-appropriate settings.

04

### Transfer the design
Sublimation color enters suitable polyester fibers while the materials pass through controlled contact.

05

### Cool & collect
Allow material handling and cooling, then collect or rewind as appropriate for the setup.

06

### Cut & sew
Cut the transferred fabric into approved garment panels, sort by size and order, then continue to assembly.

Loading, alignment and feeding preparation · Actual workshop photograph

### Preparation is part of the process
Confirm material orientation, paper layout, consistent feeding and artwork alignment before running the order. The loading photographs show preparation; they do not establish a measured production speed or a particular temperature setting.
For other garment constructions, the sequence may differ. The team confirms the route against the approved sample.

ROTARY TRANSFER FAQ

## Questions buyers ask

What does a rotary heat transfer machine do?
Also called a sublimation calender machine, it brings printed sublimation transfer paper and suitable polyester fabric through a heated drum and pressure system. Controlled contact, heat and synchronized feeding transfer the design from the paper into the polyester fibers.
How does it differ from a digital sublimation printer?
The digital printer prints the artwork onto sublimation transfer paper. The rotary heat transfer machine transfers that artwork from the paper to the fabric. Cutting equipment then separates the printed fabric into garment panels according to the approved production route.
Is this a flatbed heat press?
No. The equipment shown is a rotary drum transfer machine used for continuous fabric and transfer-paper feeding. A single-piece flatbed heat press uses a different material-handling arrangement. The appropriate process depends on the garment and production plan.
Which garments can use this process?
Suitable polyester fabrics can be used for football, basketball and American football jerseys, cycling and running apparel, training wear, sports sets, yoga wear, teamwear and event garments. Fabric composition, stretch, finish and garment construction must be reviewed for the specific product.
Will sublimation feel soft and withstand washing?
Sublimation colors suitable polyester fibers rather than adding a thick printed film. This can help retain the fabric feel and airflow, but finished softness, breathability, color and wash performance depend on the material and process. Approve a representative sample and agree any testing requirements before bulk production.
What temperature, speed and pressure does TONTON use?
Settings depend on the selected fabric, ink, transfer paper and equipment. This page does not publish an unverified temperature, speed, pressure or hourly capacity. The team reviews the production setup and sample results for each project.
Who provides this custom sportswear production service?
TONTON — Tontonsports (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. — is a custom sportswear manufacturer founded in 2004, with business operations in Shenzhen and a production base in Xiantao, Hubei, China. Its OEM/ODM production supports brands, academies, clubs and teams, including custom rash guards, MMA and BJJ shorts, training shorts and teamwear.

Equipment identification, four factory photographs and three process videos supplied by TONTON · Reviewed 21 October 2026. Machine model, temperature, pressure, speed, production capacity and project test results are confirmed separately.

THE MANUFACTURER BEHIND THE PROCESS

## Custom sportswear manufacturing at TONTON, China
TONTON — Tontonsports (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. — was founded in 2004, with business operations in Shenzhen and a production base in Xiantao, Hubei, China. Fabric cutting connects approved garment patterns with our OEM/ODM production for brands, academies, clubs and teams.

## Follow the pattern through the fabric lay
Also known as a portable electric fabric cutter or garment straight knife cutting machine.

Guided cutting at the table · Actual workshop photograph

### How the cutting action works
An electric motor drives the blade in a rapid reciprocating motion. The operator holds the handle and guides the machine along the prepared cutting line, while the base supports movement over the cutting table.

### Components for custom sportswear

- Garment fronts, backs and sleeves.

- Shorts and trouser panels.

- Collars, plackets and shaped insert panels.

- Other suitable fabric components in the approved pattern.
Material suitability, lay height and detailed machine settings are confirmed for each project. No model-specific speed, layer count or cutting tolerance is inferred from the photographs.

02 / FROM FABRIC TO PANELS

## A practical cutting workflow

01

### Prepare the fabric
Review the selected material and lay it on the cutting table with the required orientation.

02

### Position the pattern
Use an approved pattern, marker or cutting lines, allowing for size and seam requirements.

03

### Review the lay
Check alignment, fabric movement and the cutting route before starting.

04

### Guide the machine
A trained operator directs the electric cutter along the planned lines.

05

### Separate & identify
Sort the cut components by order, size and panel type.

06

### Review & hand off
Check panel completeness and matching before decoration or sewing, according to the production plan.

### The garment determines the production route
Sublimated products may be cut after heat transfer; other garments may be cut before decoration. Confirm pattern revision, stretch direction, print alignment where applicable and panel quantities before bulk cutting.

04 / TWO CUTTING ROUTES

## Operator guidance and computer-controlled paths
Both prepare garment components. Their path control and preparation differ.

Compare fabric cutting methods and production rolesReview point | Electric straight knife cutting | Computerized automatic cutting |
Cutting path | The operator guides the portable machine. | A controlled cutting head follows digital paths. |
Preparation | Approved patterns, markers or cutting lines on a prepared fabric lay. | Approved CAD patterns and a digital marker layout. |
Production choice | Review fabric, stretch, panel geometry, quantities, artwork alignment and the agreed production plan. |
Buyer approval | Confirm the sample, size chart, pattern revision and project specifications before bulk production. |

CUTTING FAQ

## Questions buyers ask

Which manufacturer provides this custom sportswear cutting process?
TONTON — Tontonsports (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. — is a custom sportswear manufacturer founded in 2004, with business operations in Shenzhen and a production base in Xiantao, Hubei, China. Fabric cutting is part of its OEM/ODM garment production for brands, academies, clubs and teams. Products include custom rash guards, MMA and BJJ shorts, training shorts and teamwear.
What is an electric straight knife fabric cutting machine?
It is a portable, operator-guided garment cutting machine. An electric motor drives a straight blade in a rapid up-and-down motion while the operator guides the machine along the approved pattern or marked cutting line.
Can it cut several fabric layers at once?
Straight knife cutting can prepare multiple laid fabric layers in one operation. The suitable lay height and number of layers depend on the material and machine configuration; TONTON confirms those details for the project rather than publishing an unverified capacity.
Which garment pieces can be prepared?
Depending on the approved pattern and material, applications include fronts, backs, sleeves, shorts and trouser panels, collars, plackets, sportswear insert panels and suitable fabric trim components.
How is it different from computerized automatic cutting?
With this machine, an operator guides the cutting path along a pattern or marked line. Computerized cutting follows digital patterns and marker layouts through a controlled cutting head. The appropriate route depends on the fabric, garment construction, quantities and production plan.
Are the photographs and videos the same kind of evidence?
The three photographs show the TONTON workshop and equipment. The two supplied videos are labelled as demonstrations; they are not evidence of a specific machine model, measured cutting performance or verified production parameters.
What should I provide for a custom sportswear order?
Share the garment type, size chart, quantities by size, fabric requirements, artwork or reference sample and delivery needs. Final artwork or CAD files are not required to begin the discussion; sample and specification approval come before bulk production.

Equipment identification and media supplied by TONTON · Reviewed 21 October 2026. Three actual workshop photographs and two labelled demonstration videos. Project specifications and equipment settings are confirmed separately.

# Computerized Automatic Fabric Cutting
From digital patterns to garment panels.
TONTON’s CNC garment cutting equipment follows approved CAD patterns and marker layouts to prepare sportswear components for the next production step. Explore the machine, the panel layouts and three actual workshop videos.

EquipmentWorkflowVideosApplicationsPanel checksPrepare your order01 / EQUIPMENT & FUNCTION

## A cutting table guided by the garment layout
The equipment prepares the shapes that become garment fronts, backs, sleeves and other specified components.

Cutting head and guide rail · Supplied equipment detail

### What the workshop material shows

- A broad, flat cutting table with garment shapes arranged across the material.

- A moving cutting head carried along controlled rails.

- Cable protection and a computer-controlled workstation.

- Printed panels prepared for cutting and subsequent assembly.
The exact blade type, model, speed, cutting tolerance and number of layers are not specified here. Drilling, punching and marking tools need separate configuration confirmation.

02 / CAD TO CUT PANELS

## Confirm the pattern. Plan the route. Cut the panels.

01

### Patterns & grading
Develop and approve garment shapes, sizes, seam allowances and relevant construction details.

02

### Marker layout
Arrange the panels for the fabric width, direction and size quantities. Layout planning supports material use; the result depends on the project.

03

### Material preparation
Prepare the selected fabric and confirm its orientation and printed layout where applicable.

04

### Computer-controlled cutting
Follow the approved digital paths to prepare the required garment components.

05

### Sorting & matching
Identify pieces by order, size and panel before handing them to the next operation.

06

### Decoration or assembly
Continue through the production route agreed for the garment.

### Printing and cutting are not always in the same order
For a sublimated panel route: design → print transfer paper → heat transfer onto fabric → cut panels → sew. Other products may be cut before embroidery, printing or assembly. The actual sequence depends on the approved material and construction.

Required components, identification, cut edges and quantities.

CUTTING FAQ

## Questions buyers ask

What is a computerized automatic fabric cutting machine?
It follows a digital garment pattern and marker layout to cut fabric into components such as fronts, backs, sleeves and other shaped panels. TONTON uses computerized cutting equipment as part of its custom sportswear production.
Is this equipment described as a laser cutter?
No. TONTON identifies this equipment as a computerized automatic cutting machine, also called a CNC garment cutting machine. This page does not claim a laser cutting mechanism. The exact blade type and optional attachments require model and configuration confirmation.
Does printing always happen after cutting?
No. For sublimated sportswear, designs can be printed onto transfer paper, transferred to fabric and then cut into garment panels. Other products may be cut before decoration. The sequence follows the approved material, construction and decoration route.
Which sportswear panels can be prepared?
Applications include panels for football, basketball, American football, running, cycling and training garments, teamwear and other suitable sportswear. Fabric, stretch, panel geometry and the production setup must be reviewed for each project.
Can the machine also drill, mark or punch fabric?
Those functions depend on the installed tools and equipment configuration. They are not confirmed from the supplied photographs or videos. Share the required notch, hole or marking detail so the team can confirm the appropriate process.
What should a buyer approve before bulk cutting?
Confirm the pattern and size chart, grading, fabric, stretch direction, seam allowances, printed artwork alignment where applicable, panel identifiers and size quantities. Review the sample and agree any dimensional tolerances before bulk production.

Equipment identification and media supplied by TONTON · Reviewed 21 October 2026. This page describes computerized automatic garment cutting; exact tool configurations and project specifications are confirmed separately.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What custom sportswear can TONTON produce?
We work on custom fight wear, teamwear, activewear, gymwear and related sportswear projects. The exact product range is confirmed around your design and project brief.
Can you add our logo and support OEM or ODM work?
Yes. Share your logo, artwork and requirements so our design and production team can confirm the suitable customization route for your project.
How do you confirm MOQ and repeat orders?
MOQ and repeat-order terms depend on the product, customization details and production plan. We confirm them with you before the order is finalized.
Can you help with colors, labels and packaging?
We can review color direction, labels and packaging requirements as part of the project brief and confirm the available options for your order.
What artwork files should we send?
Please send your logo, design references and any available artwork files through the inquiry form. Our team will review the materials and advise on the next step.
How are sampling and production timing confirmed?
Sampling and bulk-production timing are confirmed after the product, artwork and order details are reviewed. We will provide a project-specific schedule.
How will we receive progress updates?
We keep project communication aligned around the confirmed production plan and share updates through the agreed contact channel.
What happens if there is a delivery or after-sales issue?
Contact our team with the order details and issue description. We will review the situation and advise on the appropriate next step.

DEVELOPMENT PARTNER

## More clarity.
Fewer production surprises.

Good custom manufacturing starts before the first garment is sewn. TONTON helps buyers define the product, prepare artwork, select materials, review a sample, and keep the approved details connected to production.
Whether you are launching a brand, building a gym uniform, or organizing a repeat team order, our service is designed to make decisions visible and communication practical.

01

### Product planning
Clarify the garment, intended use, quantity, fit, budget, and delivery priorities.

02

### Artwork support
Turn logos, colors, references, and brand guidelines into a production-ready visual direction.

03

### Material guidance
Match fabric weight, stretch, breathability, hand feel, and durability to the product.

04

### Sample development
Confirm construction, sizing, print placement, and finish before bulk production begins.

SIX-STEP CUSTOM ROUTE

## One process.
Six clear decisions.

Every stage has a practical purpose: define what is needed, confirm it visually and physically, then manufacture against an approved direction.

STEP 01Define the brief

### Choose your product and project direction
Tell us what you are making, who will wear it, the expected quantities, target market, and required delivery window. Our team turns the initial request into a clear development brief.

STEP 02Develop the design

### Build artwork around your brand
Share vector logos, brand colors, sketches, or reference images. We support layout development and provide a digital mockup so placement, scale, and color direction can be reviewed before sampling.

STEP 03Confirm material and fit

### Select fabric, construction, and sizing
We help compare fabric performance, stretch, weight, panel construction, and size requirements for rash guards, fight shorts, training wear, and team apparel.

STEP 04Review the sample

### Approve the product before bulk production
A physical sample allows your team to check fit, workmanship, colors, branding, and functional details. Feedback is recorded before the approved specification moves into production.

STEP 05Produce and control

### Follow a connected manufacturing route
Cutting, decoration, sewing, finishing, and inspection follow the approved project details. Production coordination keeps customization requirements visible at each control point.

STEP 06Finish and deliver

### Inspect, pack, and prepare for shipment
Finished garments are checked against the order requirements, organized for packing, and prepared for the agreed shipping route with clear order communication.

DECORATION & CONSTRUCTION

## Choose the right technique for the product.

Decoration is selected around the artwork, material, use case, finish, and order needs—not simply added at the end.

01

### Full sublimation
Artwork is transferred across performance fabric for vivid, all-over graphics with no heavy surface layer.

02

### Embroidery
Thread is stitched directly into the garment or panel for a dimensional, professional brand finish.

03

### Heat transfer
Controlled heat and pressure apply selected names, numbers, logos, and graphic details to the garment.

04

### Laser cutting
Digital cutting supports clean, repeatable panels and precise components for customized construction.

05

### Performance sewing
Operators assemble stretch panels, seams, waistbands, and functional details around movement and durability.

SUPPORT THAT CONTINUES

Production support also means keeping the important order details organized for revisions, repeat programs, and future product development.

01

### Before ordering
Product consultation, reference review, material direction, artwork preparation, and quotation support.

02

### During development
Mockup review, sample coordination, feedback tracking, and specification confirmation.

03

### During production
Order communication, customization checks, workmanship inspection, and packing confirmation.

04

### For repeat orders
Reference to approved project details so your next order starts with a clearer foundation.

# Digital Sublimation Printing for Custom Sportswear
Your artwork. Printed on paper. Transferred into polyester.
At TONTON’s Xiantao production base, our in-house industrial roll-to-roll printing equipment outputs full-color designs, team logos, player names and numbers onto sublimation transfer paper. Separate heat-transfer equipment brings the design onto the selected polyester fabric.

03 / PRINTING TO GARMENT

## How the sublimation production route works
Digital artwork → transfer-paper printing → roller heat transfer to polyester → cutting → sewing and inspection.

Paper printing · Operator and equipment at work
01–02 / APPROVE & PRINT

### Confirm the artwork, then print to paper
Approve the design version, logos, roster and size allocation. The printer outputs the garment artwork onto sublimation transfer paper.
The printed roll is an intermediate output; final color approval happens after transfer to the selected fabric.

Separate roller-transfer equipment · Workshop team at work
03 / TRANSFER TO POLYESTER

### Bring the design from paper into the fabric
The printed paper and suitable polyester fabric pass through the separate roller heat-transfer stage. Heat transfers the dye into the polyester fibers.
Review color, clarity and fabric appearance on the transferred material.

Printed panel preparation · Cutting detail
04–05 / CUT, SEW & REVIEW

### Keep the right panels with the right order
Cut the transferred fabric into garment components and match panels by order, size and personalization before sewing.
Review the finished garment against the approved specification, roster and packing requirements.
See the complete factory workflow →Explore embroidery for garment branding →

### Approve color on the transferred fabric
The printed paper is an intermediate output. Screen colors and paper appearance are not the final garment approval reference. Review the design after transfer onto the selected fabric, then check the relevant garment sample.

04 / APPLICATIONS & PERSONALIZATION

## Built for complex artwork and individual team identities
Digital artwork can change between pieces, supporting all-over designs, gradients and personalized teamwear without making a separate printing screen for every color.

### Team & event apparel
Football and soccer kits, basketball uniforms, American football apparel, school teamwear, supporter jerseys and event clothing.

### Performance sportswear
Cycling, running and training apparel, sports sets, leggings and other styles where the selected polyester material and garment construction suit sublimation.

### Samples & custom runs
Develop complex prints and test personalized designs before bulk production. Confirm the complete garment MOQ, sample plan and timing for your project.

Full-color output · Contrasting graphics and panel artwork
ONE TEAM · INDIVIDUAL DETAILS

### What can change from garment to garment?
Player names · numbers · team crests · sponsor logos · approved color combinations.
Size and fit are confirmed through garment patterns and the order allocation. A different cut or silhouette needs its own development review.

Material suitability comes first: confirm polyester content, fabric color, stretch, heat tolerance and the final transferred result. Do not assume this paper-transfer route is suitable for untreated cotton or every fabric blend.

05 / QUALITY REVIEW

## The details to confirm before a print becomes an order
Use the approved artwork and sample as the reference. The following points form a practical review checklist to agree with the production team.

Printhead detail · A closer view of the paper-printing stage
ARTWORK → PAPER → FABRIC → GARMENT

### Follow the result through each stage
Start with the correct artwork and personalization list. Review the printed output, then the transferred fabric, and finally the assembled garment.
The checklist below helps align the review with your approved sample.

Review points for your sublimation projectStage | Review focus | Why it matters |
Artwork & roster | Version, spelling, numbers, sponsor logos, sizes and panel placement. | A clearly printed design still needs to match the correct person and order. |
Paper output | Visible banding, missing image areas, sharpness, alignment and consistent feed. | Identify print defects before the separate transfer stage. |
Transferred fabric | Color against the approved sample, image clarity, ghosting, fabric appearance and distortion. | The transferred fabric shows the result the garment will carry. |
Cutting & assembly | Panel identity, print position, size matching and joins across the garment. | Keep the artwork and personalization aligned through sewing. |
Finished garment | Appearance, measurements, roster counts, labels and required performance tests. | Review the complete product before packing and dispatch. |

### Soft feel and durability depend on the complete process
With a suitable polyester fabric and correctly matched process, sublimation dye enters the fibers rather than creating a separate surface film. This can preserve the fabric’s feel without a film layer that peels or cracks.
Wash fastness, rubbing fastness and color retention depend on the fabric, ink, transfer conditions and garment care. Agree any test method and acceptance criteria before production; no universal wash-cycle or fastness rating is claimed here.

PRINTING FAQ

## Questions buyers ask

What does TONTON’s digital sublimation printer do?
Our in-house industrial roll-to-roll printer prints full-color sportswear artwork, logos, names and numbers onto sublimation transfer paper. Separate roller heat-transfer equipment then transfers that design onto suitable polyester fabric before cutting and sewing.
Is this direct-to-fabric printing?
The process described here prints onto transfer paper first. The paper-to-polyester transfer is a separate heat-transfer stage. The printer itself does not cut, sew or embroider the garment.
Can every garment have a different name or number?
Yes. The print artwork can vary by garment, including names, numbers, team crests, sponsor logos and color combinations. Confirm the final roster, spelling, sizes and artwork before output. Different fits or patterns require separate garment-development approval.
Which fabrics and products are suitable?
This route is intended for suitable polyester fabrics and polyester-based performance materials confirmed through sampling. Applications include football, basketball and American football teamwear, cycling and running apparel, training kits and other compatible custom sportswear. Do not assume every fabric blend or stretch fabric uses the same transfer settings.
Does sublimation printing peel or crack?
In a correctly matched sublimation process, dye enters the polyester fibers rather than forming a separate printed film on the surface. The result can retain a soft fabric feel without a film layer that peels or cracks. Wash and rubbing performance still depend on the fabric, ink, transfer process and care conditions; confirm any required tests on the finished sample.
Is digital sublimation suitable for samples and small orders?
Digital output does not require a separate screen for each printed color, making it suitable for complex artwork, sample development and personalized small runs. Garment MOQ, sample cost and timing depend on the complete product and must be confirmed with the team.
What should I send before printing starts?
Send your artwork or references, logo files, color targets, placement instructions, names and numbers, product type, fabric direction and quantities by size. Confirm the final artwork and the relevant transferred-fabric or garment sample before bulk production.

Process background: Epson’s explanation of dye-sublimation printing. This reference explains the general process and does not identify the brand of TONTON’s equipment.

# Multi-Head Embroidery for Custom Teamwear
Team identity, built stitch by stitch.

EquipmentProcessVideosApplicationsQualityPrepare your order01 / MACHINES, NEEDLES & THREAD

## One approved design. Multiple working heads.
Each head carries a set of needles and colored threads. The embroidery program controls stitch movement and color changes; multiple heads can work on repeated versions of the same design.

Machine heads. Needles and thread controls arranged across the production line.
Thread colors. Color selection follows the approved design and sample.
Repeated production. Parallel heads support repeat embroidery work.

JIAYU branding is visible in the supplied material. Ask the team for project-specific equipment information; no exact model, speed or head-count claim is made here.

Confirm artwork, finished dimensions, placement and thread colors. Digitizing defines the stitch paths and sequence; the fabric and design guide the stabilizer and setup choices.

Embroidery production · Machine heads and garment panels

Use the confirmed embroidery program, thread colors and placement. Multi-head production repeats the design across prepared panels or suitable garments.

Garment panels at the embroidery line · Actual photograph

### Special finishes need a separate capability check
Chenille or towel embroidery, 3D foam embroidery and cap embroidery require the appropriate equipment, attachments and setup. Their availability cannot be established from standard multi-head machine photographs alone.
Send a reference of the effect you want. The team will confirm the route and sample rather than treating every technique as interchangeable.

05 / SAMPLE & QUALITY REVIEW

## Look beyond the front of the logo
Agree the inspection points for your project. These are buyer review considerations, not a claim of a published test result or a fixed factory inspection standard.

### Artwork & color
Correct design version, spelling, dimensions, placement and thread-color reference.

### Stitch appearance
Letter clarity, outline registration, coverage, loose threads and clean finishing.

### Fabric & reverse side
Puckering, distortion, backing visibility, stretch and comfort against the skin.

### Order matching
Correct panel, size, name or number, plus the required quantities.

### Test the selected performance fabric
Lightweight or stretchy fabrics need a suitable design and stabilizer. Review the sewn result on the intended material, including stretch and skin contact. For close-fitting rash guards, confirm whether embroidery, a patch or sublimation best suits the proposed area.

EMBROIDERY FAQ

## Questions buyers ask

What does a computerized multi-head embroidery machine do?
It follows a digitized embroidery program to stitch thread into a selected fabric or garment panel. Multiple heads can repeat the same approved design in parallel, while programmed needle changes select the required thread colors.
What embroidery equipment is shown in TONTON’s workshop?
The supplied workshop photographs and machine video show multi-head embroidery equipment with visible JIAYU branding. Exact model, head count, embroidery field, needle count and production speed are not specified on this page.
Can TONTON embroider team logos, names and numbers?
Team crests, brand logos, lettering, names and numbers can be developed for embroidery, subject to the design, size, fabric and placement. Personalized names and numbers need an approved roster and a suitable production plan; different heads should not be assumed to stitch different designs simultaneously.
Can the pictured machines make chenille, 3D foam embroidery or embroidered caps?
These techniques depend on the machine configuration, attachments, materials and setup. The pictured standard embroidery heads alone do not confirm chenille, 3D foam or cap capability. Send the required effect and product so the team can confirm the process and sample.
Can embroidery be used on stretch sportswear?
Suitability depends on the fabric, design size, stitch density, stabilizer and placement. Review a sew-out on the selected material for puckering, stretch, backing visibility and comfort against the skin. Do not assume the same embroidery setup suits every rash guard, jersey or performance fabric.
What should I approve before bulk embroidery?
Confirm the artwork version, finished size, placement, thread colors, fabric or panel, backing approach and any names or numbers. Review a physical stitch sample on the intended material before approving the bulk production setup.

Workshop overview · Supplied factory photograph

## Factory Questions Buyers Ask
Where is the TONTON factory?
Our production base is at No. 121, Xianyuan Blvd, Xiantao City, Hubei Province, 433000, China. TONTON was founded in Shenzhen in 2004 and maintains Shenzhen business operations.
What does TONTON manufacture?
TONTON manufactures custom team sportswear, including rash guards, BJJ and MMA shorts, training shorts and other teamwear. We support OEM projects from buyer specifications and ODM development from product references.
Does every order use every production process?
No. The route depends on the approved fabric, garment construction and decoration. Printing, transfer, embroidery and cutting methods are selected for the specific product.
What should I approve before bulk production?
Confirm the product specification, artwork version, fabric, fit, size quantities, branding and sample details. The team then confirms the production and inspection plan.
Can I review factory photos, documents and project references?
This page includes real factory photographs, document links and routes to product and customer references. Ask the team for additional process photographs or videos relevant to your project.

ABOUT TONTON

# Company Profile
& Chairman
TONTON is our brand. Our public-facing company name is Tontonsports (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. Our business began in Shenzhen in 2004. We help brands, gyms, academies, clubs, teams and retailers develop products from the initial brief through sampling, production review and packing.
Inspect the FactoryBuild Your Project Brief

TONTON SPORTSWEAR

## B2B CUSTOM FIGHTWEAR & PERFORMANCE APPAREL MANUFACTURER

FOUNDER & CHAIRMAN

## The person behind TONTON
Meet Peter Hu through real company photographs, interviews and published reporting.
FOUNDER & CHAIRMAN

### Peter Hu / Hu Xinzhen
Peter Hu (Hu Xinzhen) is the founder and chairman of TONTON. His work connects custom sportswear manufacturing with international trade, e-commerce and industry knowledge sharing.
An April 2026 Xiantao Daily profile traces his move to Shenzhen in 2004 and the development of a business focused on customized team sportswear for overseas markets. It also describes TONTON’s participation in the 2014 Alibaba commemorative clothing project.
The same profile records his industry teaching, service as a Xiantao CPPCC member and recognition in the seventh Xiantao moral role-model awards in 2024.

EDUCATION SUPPORT

### A ten-year commitment to the community.
A municipal government report dated 26 August 2026 describes an RMB 1 million education support fund established by Hu Xinzhen for Shagengba Village. The commitment is spread over ten years, with RMB 100,000 annually; the village committee receives, manages and supervises the funds.
Read the municipal report ↗

COMPANY DEVELOPMENT

## From a Shenzhen sportswear business to connected manufacturing
A concise timeline based on company records and published reporting. It explains how TONTON's commercial operations and Hubei production base fit together.
2004TONTON began in Shenzhen with a focus on custom sportswear and international B2B orders.

2014The team took part in the Chinese supplier network that completed 130,000 Alibaba listing commemorative garments in 12 days.

2023TONTON established its Hubei manufacturing company and expanded production in Xiantao.

2025Hubei Daily reported the launch of an intelligent production system using AI-assisted design, QR-tracked panels, smart sorting and hanging lines.

2026Public reporting documented further AI-supported manufacturing development and university-industry work on smart sizing and virtual fitting.

DIRECT ANSWERS

## Company & manufacturing questions
What is TONTON?
TONTON is the public brand. The company presented on this website is Tontonsports (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. TONTON began in Shenzhen in 2004 and supports B2B custom fightwear and sportswear projects.
What products does TONTON specialize in?
The website focuses on custom rash guards, MMA and BJJ shorts, grappling shorts, training shorts, teamwear and related performance sportswear programs.
Who does TONTON manufacture for?
TONTON supports fightwear brands, gyms, academies, clubs, teams, retailers and other private-label buyers.
Does TONTON support OEM and ODM projects?
Yes. Buyers can provide a completed specification or work with the team to develop product, artwork, material and construction direction before sampling.
How can a buyer verify TONTON manufacturing capabilities?
The Factory page contains real workshop imagery, production stages, quality-control information and source documents. Product pages and buyer guides provide product-specific construction evidence.

PROJECT PLANNING TOOL

# Build a production-ready custom fightwear brief
Choose the core requirements now, then send a structured summary to TONTON for a project-specific review.
BEFORE YOU SEND

## What to send — and what happens next
Start with the product, estimated quantity, intended use and contact details. Add your size range, delivery country and target date when known. A logo or reference file is optional; finished production artwork is not required to start.

AFTER YOUR REQUEST

### Your next step with TONTON
We review the brief and clarify the material, construction, artwork and sample requirements before confirming a project-specific quotation and schedule. After a successful online submission, keep the reference shown on this page for follow-up.
Using WhatsApp or email instead? Your written brief is prefilled, but attach any reference file separately in that conversation.

## What should buyers specify for a custom sublimated Rash Guard?
A custom Rash Guard brief should define the intended sport, fit, sleeve length, size range, artwork, panel layout, seam direction, fabric requirements and optional hem grip. TONTON reviews these decisions together, then confirms the final composition, weight, measurements and construction against the approved sample.

PRODUCT DIRECTION

## Build a rash guard around the way your customers train.

A strong custom rash guard program starts with use, fit, and artwork—not a generic blank garment.
TONTON supports brands, BJJ academies, MMA gyms, grappling teams, and distributors with product development for custom sublimated rash guards. We help define sleeve length, panel direction, size requirements, fabric performance, artwork placement, and packaging before the order moves forward.

01

### BJJ & grappling academies
Create a consistent team identity across adult, youth, rank, or competition programs.

02

### MMA gyms & fight teams
Develop training apparel around movement, repeat wear, and clear sponsor placement.

03

### Private-label brands
Translate a brand direction into a repeatable rash guard range with coordinated colors and graphics.

CUSTOMIZATION OPTIONS

## What can be customized on a sublimated rash guard?
Each decision is reviewed together so the visual design and garment construction support the same end use.
01

### Sleeve and fit direction
Choose short or long sleeves and define the intended fit and size range for your market.

02

### All-over artwork
Apply team colors, patterns, logos, names, and sponsor graphics across the printable panels.

03

### Fabric performance
Review stretch, hand feel, weight, and intended training conditions before sampling.

04

### Construction details
Confirm panel layout, breathable mesh, flatlock seam direction, neckline, silicone hem grip, printed labels, and other brand-specific requirements.

PERFORMANCE CONSTRUCTION

## Inspect the fabric, seams, mesh, and finishing details.

Real sample photography shows the product areas a buyer should review before approving a custom sublimated graphic Rash Guard for BJJ, MMA, grappling, or training.

Fabric direction
Polyester-spandex stretch performance fabric

Ventilation option
Underarm and side mesh panel

Seam direction
Low-profile flatlock construction

Hem option
Silicone anti-slip grip

01

### Performance fabric and panel fit
The complete sample shows a smooth stretch body, raglan sleeve direction, close neckline, and clean areas for custom sublimated graphics or logos.

02

### Breathable side mesh panel
A perforated side insert can add ventilation through the underarm and torso area while preserving a close performance silhouette.

03

### Flatlock raglan seam
Low-profile stretch stitching follows the sleeve and body panel lines to create a clean construction direction for high-movement training use.

04

### Mesh-to-fabric transition
The sample makes the alignment between solid stretch fabric, ventilating mesh, vertical joining seam, and lower hem easy to inspect.

05

### Silicone anti-slip hem option
A silicone grip at the inside hem can help limit ride-up. Grip width, placement, and final construction are confirmed during sampling.

06

### Tagless printed neck label
The physical sample shows an 85% polyester and 15% spandex fabric label printed inside the neck. Composition and care copy are finalized for each approved project.

FABRIC DIRECTION

## Rash Guard fabric should balance stretch, recovery, and print clarity.
We commonly evaluate polyester-spandex performance directions for sublimated Rash Guards. Final composition, weight, hand feel, and stretch are confirmed against the approved sample and project requirements.

### Multi-directional stretch
Supports close-fit movement for BJJ, MMA, grappling, and training applications.

### Shape recovery
Helps the garment return toward its intended fit after repeated movement and wear.

### Smooth print surface
Supports clear gradients, detailed graphics, sponsor marks, and team colors.

### Project-specific GSM
Fabric weight is selected and confirmed during development instead of being presented as one universal specification.

RASH GUARD CRAFT

## How a sublimated Rash Guard moves from artwork to inspection.
01

### Artwork and color preparation
Logos, pattern scale, sponsor marks, and panel placements are organized in the digital mockup.

02

### Sublimation transfer
Approved artwork is transferred into compatible performance fabric for an integrated, lightweight graphic result.

03

### Panel cutting
Printed pieces are cut to the approved pattern with artwork position and panel direction in view.

04

### Stretch-garment sewing
The neckline, sleeves, body panels, and hems are assembled using construction suited to the selected stretch fabric.

05

### Finished-garment inspection
Measurements, seams, visual placement, color, labeling, and workmanship are reviewed before packing.

A practical OEM route for custom BJJ and MMA rash guards, with key decisions confirmed before bulk work begins.

### Define the product brief

04

### Produce, inspect, and deliver
Production follows the approved details, followed by finished-garment inspection, packing, and shipment preparation.

BUYER FAQ

## Custom rash guard questions buyers ask before ordering
Clear answers for brands, gyms, academies, teams, distributors, and private-label buyers.
Read Buyer Resources →Build Your Project Brief →

01What information should I send for a custom rash guard quote?
Send the required quantity, short- or long-sleeve preference, target users, size range, artwork or logo files, and any reference products. These details help us define the development brief and confirm the next step.
02Can TONTON make rash guards for BJJ academies and MMA teams?
Yes. We support custom rash guard programs for BJJ academies, MMA gyms, grappling teams, brands, and distributors. Team colors, sponsor marks, names, and coordinated designs can be reviewed during artwork development.
03What is the MOQ for custom sublimated rash guards?
Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. The final order structure is confirmed against the style, size breakdown, artwork, and other project requirements.
04Can I customize both long-sleeve and short-sleeve rash guards?
Yes. Sleeve length is one of the first product decisions. We can review short- and long-sleeve directions, along with fit, panel layout, sizing, and artwork placement.
05Will sublimated graphics peel or create a heavy print layer?
Sublimation transfers the artwork into compatible performance fabric rather than adding a thick surface print. It is suited to detailed, all-over graphics and avoids a heavy printed layer on the garment.
06Can I review a mockup and sample before bulk production?
Yes. A digital mockup is used to review the visual direction, and sample development can be used to confirm fit, construction, color, and branding before bulk production.
07Which artwork files are best for production?
Vector logo and artwork files are preferred because they support clean scaling and placement. Brand colors, fonts, sponsor marks, and reference images are also helpful when preparing the mockup.
08What fabric is used for a custom Rash Guard?
A Rash Guard is typically developed with a smooth polyester-spandex performance fabric selected for stretch, recovery, print compatibility, and next-to-skin comfort. The exact fiber ratio and fabric weight are confirmed for the selected project rather than assumed from a generic specification.
09How is a sublimated Rash Guard manufactured?
After the artwork and color direction are approved, the design is transferred into compatible fabric, the printed panels are cut, stretch seams and the neckline are assembled, and the finished Rash Guard is inspected for workmanship, measurements, color, and branding.
010Can a custom Rash Guard include mesh panels, flatlock seams, and a silicone hem grip?
Yes. These construction directions can be reviewed during development. Mesh placement, seam type, hem finish, and anti-slip silicone grip should be confirmed against the intended fit, fabric, and approved sample before bulk production.

QUICK ANSWER

## What defines a custom functional training short?
A functional training short combines the intended fit and length with a suitable stretch-woven fabric, secure waistband, pocket direction, ventilation, crotch mobility and reinforced finishing. TONTON confirms the final material, construction, logo method and performance checks on the approved sample instead of assuming one universal specification.

CONTENT REVIEW

### Reviewed by TONTON Product Development & Quality Control Team
Based on physical sample inspection, confirmed product specifications, and current TONTON development and production workflows. Project-specific values remain subject to sample approval.Last reviewed: September 22, 2026Inspect Factory Evidence →Review Production Support →Build Your Project Brief →
PRODUCT DIRECTION

## One training short for gym, combat conditioning, outdoor movement, and utility wear.

This is a multi-purpose functional short—not a single-purpose MMA competition short.
TONTON helps brands, gyms, teams, and distributors develop this silhouette around the intended market. We review woven fabric direction, stretch and recovery, waistband adjustment, zip-pocket construction, ventilation, crotch mobility, reinforced stitching, branding, and size range before the sample is approved.

01

### Fitness & combat brands
Build a versatile private-label short for gym work, HIIT, boxing drills, and combat conditioning.

02

### Outdoor & utility labels
Develop a lightweight tactical direction with ventilation, secure storage, and an adjustable fit.

03

### Gyms, teams & retailers
Coordinate market-specific colors, size ranges, logos, and construction details for repeat programs.

CUSTOMIZATION OPTIONS

## Customize the functional system—not only the color and logo.
Fabric, waistband security, pocket placement, ventilation, seam reinforcement, and branding should be developed as one connected specification.
01

### Woven fabric direction
Compare lightweight polyester-elastane, nylon-elastane, or blended stretch-woven directions against the intended hand feel and movement.

02

### Adjustable waistband
Review elastic support, hook-and-loop adjustment, internal drawcord, comfort, and branded waist details.

03

### Pocket and ventilation
Confirm the zip-pocket opening, storage requirement, perforation layout, edge finish, and placement.

04

### Fit, reinforcement and branding
Define the athletic silhouette, crotch mobility, hem finish, stress-point reinforcement, and approved logo method.

FUNCTIONAL PRODUCT CONSTRUCTION

## Technical details built for movement and everyday utility.

This reference combines a light, structured woven direction with adjustable waist support, secure storage, airflow details, shaped panel lines, and reinforced finishing. Final composition, weight, stretch, and trim specifications are confirmed against the approved sample.

WOVENLightweight performance fabric direction
