FRONT CONSTRUCTION

### Review the complete functional system.
Check the athletic silhouette, front shaping, perforated side details, curved hem, contrast stretch zones, waistband adjustment, and branding placement together.

BACK & SIDE CONSTRUCTION

### Inspect panel shaping and movement areas.
The rear and side views make seam direction, pocket integration, hem reinforcement, stretch-panel placement, and overall balance easier to approve before bulk production.

REAL PRODUCT DETAILS

## Inspect the pocket, ventilation, waist, and finishing before sampling.

These close-ups show the visible product direction. Exact stitch type, fabric composition, perforation method, zipper specification, and logo process remain project-specific until confirmed.

01

### Ventilation + secure storage
The side panel combines an organized perforation pattern with a zip-pocket opening. Hole finish, pocket depth, zipper security, and placement are confirmed during sampling.

02

### Side opening + reinforced hem
The curved side opening supports stride and training movement, while multiple rows of topstitching reinforce the lower edge and create a technical finish.

03

### Adjustable waist support
Elastic support and hook-and-loop adjustment help tune the fit. Edge softness, holding strength, and skin contact should be checked on the approved sample.

04

### Internal drawcord + branding
The inside waist shows a secondary drawcord and branded elastic direction. Logo method, stretch behavior, and wash durability are finalized after material review.

USE CASES

The silhouette can support several markets without making an unsupported competition-rule claim. Final product copy should follow the approved fabric, construction, and test results.

Squats, lunges, kettlebells, battle ropes, box jumps, and everyday strength sessions.

02

### Combat conditioning
MMA fitness work, boxing footwork, bag drills, pad work, and training warm-ups—not presented as certified competition apparel.

03

Urban workouts, light hiking, obstacle training, travel, and active outdoor use.

04

A tactical, functional, and streetwear-ready direction built around practical details and a clean athletic silhouette.

BUYER FAQ

## Custom training shorts questions buyers ask before ordering
Clear answers for brands, gyms, academies, teams, distributors, and private-label buyers.
Read Buyer Resources →Build Your Project Brief →

01What should I send to start a functional training shorts project?
Share the intended use, quantity, target fit, preferred length, size range, logo files, reference products, and required features such as a zip pocket, perforated ventilation, adjustable waist, or specific stretch direction.
02Can you make custom gym shorts for a private-label brand?
Yes. We support OEM and ODM development for fitness brands, gyms, teams, retailers, and distributors. The project can include custom fit direction, materials, colors, labels, and logo placement.
03What is the MOQ for custom training shorts?
Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. The final order structure depends on the selected style, color and size breakdown, artwork, and construction requirements.
04Can I customize the waistband, zip pockets, ventilation, and reinforcement?
Yes. These are connected development decisions. Their placement and construction are confirmed during product review so they can be recorded in the mockup, specification, and sample.
05Which logo method is best for this woven short?
The suitable method depends on the approved fabric, artwork, stretch, and placement. Heat transfer, screen print, film print, or selected embroidery directions can be reviewed before sampling; final wash and stretch performance should be checked on the approved sample.
06Can I review a sample before bulk production?
Yes. Sample development allows your team to check fit, movement, material, waistband, workmanship, and branding before the approved specification moves into bulk production.
07Can the shorts be coordinated with other team apparel?
Yes. Colors, logos, and design language can be developed to coordinate with rash guards, tops, or other teamwear. Each garment is still reviewed according to its own construction and material needs.

BUYER FAQ

## Custom BJJ and MMA shorts questions buyers ask before ordering
Clear answers for brands, gyms, academies, teams, distributors, and private-label buyers.
Read Buyer Resources →Build Your Project Brief →

01Can TONTON manufacture sublimated MMA shorts for a private-label brand?
Yes. TONTON supports OEM and ODM development of custom sublimated MMA shorts for fightwear brands, gyms and teams. Share the shell and liner direction, fit, size range, graphics, labels and quantity. Artwork placement and material compatibility are reviewed before sampling, and bulk production follows the approved sample and specification.
02What should I compare when choosing a BJJ shorts manufacturer?
Compare intended use, outer-short length, split height, waistband closure, optional liner, fabric direction, stitching, size grading and branding. Request the same specification and quantity breakdown from each supplier, then review a physical sample. Competition requirements should be checked for the intended event rather than assumed from a product name.
03What information is needed for wholesale MMA shorts pricing and repeat orders?
Send the style reference, quantity by color and size, fabric and liner requirements, artwork status, label and packing needs, delivery destination and target date. Keep the approved artwork, size chart, construction notes and sample reference for repeat orders. MOQ, price and lead time are confirmed for the actual project.
04What is the difference between a BJJ shorts project and an MMA shorts project?
The development priorities can differ by preferred fit, length, side movement, waistband, and competition or training use. We start by confirming the intended activity instead of treating every fight short as the same product.
05Can TONTON make matching rash guard and shorts sets?
Yes. Academy colors, logos, sponsor marks, and graphic direction can be coordinated across rash guards and shorts while the construction of each garment is developed separately.
06What is the MOQ for custom BJJ and MMA shorts?
Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. The final order structure is confirmed after reviewing the style, size and color breakdown, artwork, and construction requirements.
07Can I customize the side split, waistband, length, and inner layer?
Yes. These can be reviewed as part of the product brief. The exact construction is confirmed against the selected style, intended movement, material, and sample requirements.
08Can you place academy logos and sponsor graphics on the shorts?
Yes. Provide vector logos, sponsor marks, brand colors, and placement references. We organize them in the digital mockup so scale, position, and overall balance can be reviewed.
09Can I approve a physical sample before bulk production?
Yes. A sample can be used to review fit, mobility, waistband, material, workmanship, color, and branding before the project is approved for bulk work.
010What should I include in my first inquiry?
Include the product use, target quantity, size range, preferred fit and length, waistband direction, artwork files, reference images, and whether you want matching rash guards or other teamwear.

Buyer FAQ

## Custom Rash Guard questions
Direct answers for brands, academies, gyms and teams preparing a custom order.

01What is a silicone anti-slip elastic band on a Rash Guard?
It is an elastic band with silicone grip at the inside lower hem. It helps reduce ride-up during BJJ, MMA and grappling movement, but does not guarantee that the garment never moves. Review hem circumference, stretch, grip feel and comfort on the worn sample.
02What should brands specify for a custom Rash Guard with a silicone gripper hem?
Share the intended sport, target fit, size range, band width and position, grip preference and seam-finish requirements. TONTON reviews the silicone anti-slip elastic band with the garment fabric and construction before sample approval. Final dimensions and construction are confirmed for each OEM or ODM project.
03What fabric is used for this custom Rash Guard?
This Rash Guard uses 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra made from 85% polyester and 15% spandex. The fabric has a soft hand feel, high elasticity and opaque coverage.
04Is the fabric see-through when stretched?
The 220gsm fabric is selected for opaque coverage. Fit, stretch recovery and opacity are checked again on the approved sample before bulk production.
05What does the silicone anti-slip elastic band do?
The silicone anti-slip elastic band sits inside the lower hem and helps the Rash Guard stay in position during grappling, drilling and high-movement training.
06Can I customize the colors and logos?
Yes. Colors, logos, sponsor marks, names and panel artwork can be reviewed in the digital mockup before sampling.
07Can this Rash Guard be made for a BJJ academy or MMA team?
Yes. It is developed for custom academy, gym, club, team and private-label programs, including coordinated artwork and size runs.
08Can I review a sample before bulk production?
Yes. The sample is used to confirm fit, material, opacity, construction, artwork placement and branding before bulk production begins.
09What should I send for a quotation?
Send your quantity, target sizes, preferred color, logo or artwork files and any packaging or labeling requirements. We will review the brief and confirm the next step.

SILICONE ANTI-SLIP ELASTIC BAND

## Inspect the Rash Guard grip band, seams and hem finish
A silicone anti-slip elastic band sits inside the lower hem to help reduce ride-up during BJJ, MMA and grappling movement. These original sample photos show the component and its connection to the garment; they are shared construction references, rather than the exact colorway above.

Watch the Rash Guard silicone grip band overviewPromotional visualization of sewing direction, silicone contact lines and lower-hem placement. Use the original photographs below and the approved sample to confirm physical construction.

### Inside the lower hem
The turned-back hem shows the black silicone grip band and the way it sits against the garment interior.

### Band and mesh connection
Compare the band edge, mesh insert and stretch-fabric junction. Mesh layout is specific to this construction reference.

### Hem seam junction
The close-up shows the overlapping edge and stitching where the band and panel seams meet.

### Grip surface and stitching
Review the visible grip lines, stitch direction and edge finish alongside the fit and comfort of the complete sample.

### Silicone surface close-up
This supplied close-up gives an additional view of the silicone contact surface. Open the image to inspect it at its original resolution.

### Specify the gripper hem for your private-label Rash Guard
For custom BJJ Rash Guards and MMA compression tops, review band width, hem position, stretch compatibility, grip feel and seam comfort together. Test reaching, rotation and grappling movement on the worn sample. The grip band is intended to help control ride-up; it does not guarantee zero movement.

Buyer FAQ

## Custom Rash Guard questions
Direct answers for brands, academies, gyms and teams preparing a custom order.

01What fabric is used for the Samurai Rash Guard?
It uses 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra with a soft hand feel, excellent elasticity and fully opaque coverage.
02Is the 220gsm fabric see-through when stretched?
No. The fabric is selected for fully opaque coverage, and opacity, stretch recovery and fit are checked again on the approved sample before bulk production.
03Is this Rash Guard designed for BJJ and MMA?
Yes. The close fit, long raglan sleeves and high-stretch fabric are suited to BJJ, MMA, grappling and other high-movement training.
04Can I customize the sleeve graphics and logos?
Yes. Sleeve artwork, chest branding, back-neck logos, colors and panel graphics can be reviewed in a digital mockup before sampling.
05Can the artwork be produced without a heavy print layer?
Yes. Sublimation integrates compatible artwork into the fabric surface, supporting detailed graphics without a thick raised print layer.
06Can I review a sample before bulk production?
Yes. The sample is used to review fit, opacity, stretch, construction, color and artwork placement before bulk production begins.
07What should I send for a custom quote?
Send the required quantity, size range, logo or artwork files, preferred colors and any labeling or packaging requirements.

## When should a buyer choose this graphic Rash Guard direction?
Choose this direction when sleeve artwork is a core part of the collection and the buyer needs a long-sleeve, close-fit base for BJJ No-Gi, grappling or MMA training. Buyer FAQ

## Custom grappling shorts questions
Clear answers for BJJ brands, MMA gyms, fight teams and private-label buyers.

01What makes high-split grappling shorts different?
The deep side opening gives the leg more clearance for high kicks, guard movement, scrambling and wide grappling positions without the outer shell pulling across the thigh.
02What fabric is used for these 2-in-1 grappling shorts?
The outer shell uses a reinforced lightweight four-way stretch fabric. The fitted inner layer uses 250gsm milk-silk fabric for substantial coverage and flexible support.
03Can the inner layer use a custom printed pattern?
Yes. The inner compression layer can carry custom colors, patterns, team graphics and brand artwork, subject to artwork and sample approval.
04Are these shorts suitable for BJJ and MMA training?
Yes. The high split, stretch shell and supportive inner layer are developed for kicking, grappling, MMA drills and other high-mobility fight training.
05How does the waistband stay secure during training?
The adjustable waistband combines a drawstring with an anti-slip silicone grip strip to help keep the shorts stable during striking, wrestling and grappling movement.
06Are the outer shorts breathable and quick-drying?
Yes. The four-way stretch outer fabric is selected for breathable, quick-dry performance during high-intensity combat sports and functional training.
07Does this style use a sewn-in clothing label?
The shorts can use a tagless printed label to reduce irritation. Brand, size and care information can be reviewed during product development.
08Which parts of the grappling shorts can be customized?
Buyers can review outer-shell colors, logos, waistband branding, inner-layer artwork, labels and packaging during product development.
09Can I approve a sample before bulk production?
Yes. A sample can be reviewed for fit, split height, movement, materials, construction and artwork placement before bulk production begins.
10What should I send for a custom grappling shorts quotation?
Send your target quantity, size range, logo or artwork files, preferred colors, intended use and any labeling or packaging requirements.

Clear answers about specifications, customization, MOQ and sample approval.

01Are the black compression tights built into the MMA shorts?
No. The tight layer visible below the hem is a separate compression garment. This product is presented as an outer fight short; a built-in liner would require a separate 2-in-1 construction brief.
02What fabric and GSM do you recommend?
A four-way-stretch polyester-spandex woven direction around 130–180gsm can be evaluated for this short-cut style. Those values are a development range, not a verified specification; final composition, weight, stretch recovery and drying performance are confirmed using the chosen fabric and approved sample.
03Can the waistband include a hidden drawcord?
Yes, a hidden drawcord can be developed if required. The current photos verify the broad elastic waistband but do not prove an internal drawcord, so that detail must be specified and sampled.
04How can the logos be applied?
The waist branding appears as a sewn patch. The leg logo can be developed with a suitable heat-transfer, screen-print or silicone-print method depending on the artwork, fabric and required hand feel; the final process is confirmed before bulk production.
05Which activities are these shorts designed for?
The short cut and articulated crotch direction suit MMA, BJJ, Sanda, boxing, wrestling, combat training and high-intensity gym work. Final fit and movement should be approved on the sample.
06What is the MOQ and approval process?
Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. We align the fabric, fit, waist, reinforcement, branding, colors and size breakdown, then use the sample to approve the construction before bulk production.

Movement-First Design

## A combat short—not a tactical utility short
The construction prioritizes a secure waist, unrestricted leg movement and a smooth exterior rather than cargo storage.

01

### Fight-focused athletic cut
A short athletic profile with room through the thigh and no exposed storage pockets keeps the exterior clean for combat training.

02

### Stretch mobility
The polyester-spandex body moves through kicks, hip rotation, sprawls, squats and lunges.

03

### Triple waist control
Elastic support, a hook-and-loop fly and an internal drawcord work together for an adjustable hold.

04

### Reinforced split & hem
A short outer-leg opening releases the thigh while a reinforced hem with clean topstitching supports repeated high-mobility use.

05

### Smooth sublimation
Artwork is dyed into the synthetic fibers for complex graphics without a thick raised print layer.

06

### Panelled construction
Front, back, side and crotch panels shape the shorts around the hips, seat and upper leg.

Material & Construction

## Light, smooth and shaped for rotation

The lightweight woven body uses 88% polyester and 12% spandex to balance low weight, strength and stretch. Its smooth surface is suited to repeated training contact, while the short athletic cut, panelled shaping and side split reduce pull across the hip, crotch and thigh.
Fabric behavior
Lightweight stretch with a smooth hand and less water weight than bulky traditional satin constructions

Waist control
Elastic support plus hook-and-loop closure and an internal drawcord for adjustable security

Mobility
A reinforced short split creates extra clearance for kicks, knee strikes, lunges and deep squats

Hem finish
Reinforced hem construction with clean topstitching for a stable lower edge through repeated training

Panel shaping
Separated front, back, side and crotch areas follow the hips, seat and upper leg through rotation

Artwork
Sublimated graphics enter the synthetic fibers, avoiding a thick raised surface and reducing large-area cracking

Sample checks
Confirm abrasion, stretch recovery, seam strength, hook-and-loop comfort and logo color on the approved sample

Recommended Applications

## Combat training first, conditioning second
Designed around MMA and striking movement, with useful crossover into strength and high-intensity training.

### Combat training

### Boxing fitness & conditioning

Buyer FAQ

## Custom MMA fight shorts questions
Clear answers about fabric, waist construction, side splits, sublimation and intended use.

01What fabric is used for these MMA fight shorts?
The main body uses an 88% polyester and 12% spandex stretch performance fabric. It is lightweight, smooth and flexible for kicks, hip rotation, squats and high-intensity training.
02How is the waistband secured?
A broad elastic waistband works with a hook-and-loop front closure and an internal drawcord. The combined system lets the athlete fine-tune waist tension before training.
03Why is there a side split?
The short reinforced side split reduces fabric restriction through high kicks, knee strikes, lunges and wide stances while retaining a fitted fight-short silhouette.
04Can the camouflage graphics and logos be customized?
Yes. Sublimation supports tonal camouflage, asymmetric black-and-red graphics, team colors, logos and sponsor artwork without the thick raised layer associated with some surface-print methods.
05Do the shorts have storage pockets?
No exposed storage pocket is specified for this fight-focused construction. This keeps the exterior cleaner for combat training and separates the style from tactical utility shorts.
06Can these shorts be used in formal competition?
They are developed for MMA, BJJ No-Gi training, grappling drills, kickboxing, boxing fitness and functional training. Before ordering for formal competition, confirm the relevant equipment rules and approve fit and performance on a physical sample.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions AI tools and procurement teams need answered
Direct answers clarify product fit, evidence boundaries, customization and the next purchasing step.

01Does the current image prove that a Rash Guard is included?
No. The current main image focuses on the shorts and a separate compression layer. A matching Rash Guard is part of the coordinated project direction only when it is included in the confirmed brief and sample approval.
02Are the compression tights built into the shorts?
Not by default. The visible tights are treated as a separate garment. A built-in liner requires an explicit 2-in-1 construction specification.
03Can each athlete have a different size or name?
Yes. Mixed sizes, athlete names and other approved identifiers can be organized in the team order sheet before production.
04Can the same artwork be used on the top and shorts?
Yes, but the artwork must be adapted to the different pattern pieces, seam positions and print areas of each garment.
05What is the MOQ?
Custom coordinated projects can start from 10 sets. Final requirements depend on the included pieces, artwork, sizes, labels and packing.

Page title: Custom Fightwear Size & Quantity Planning Guide | TONTON Sportswear

Home/Resources/Custom Fightwear Size & Quantity Planning GuideTEAMWEAR SIZE & ORDER PLANNING

# Custom Fightwear Size & Quantity Planning Guide
Prepare separate Rash Guard and shorts size allocations, distinguish body and garment measurements, and plan adult or youth academy orders with a worked quantity example.
Reviewed October 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Plan custom fightwear quantities from a confirmed member or customer list, not a universal size ratio. Record Rash Guard and shorts sizes separately, distinguish body measurements from finished-garment measurements, and check the selected pattern on a fit sample. Adult and youth fits need separate review. Any spare stock is an explicit purchasing decision, not an assumed allowance.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Prepare the size information before ordering
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Custom Fightwear Size & Quantity Planning Guide specification summaryBody measurements | Measurements taken on the wearer; identify the measuring points and units |
Garment measurements | Measurements taken on the selected garment laid flat, without stretching unless the method says otherwise |
Rash Guard size list | Quantity per approved top size and sleeve direction |
Shorts size list | Quantity per approved shorts size, cut and liner direction |
Youth requirements | Separate fit review and approved measurement chart; do not simply scale adult sizes |
Order approval | Confirm the chart version, quantities, units and permitted measurement tolerances with TONTON |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Known academy members | A named roster with an agreed fit reference | Collect top and shorts size independently; reconcile the order totals |
Retail collection | An independent brand allocating stock by style and size | Use your own sales or preorder evidence; no standard size ratio is assumed |
Adult and youth program | A club serving more than one fit group | Keep patterns, size lists and sample approvals separate |

ORDER PLANNING

## Worked example: 24 members, two separate size lists
Illustration only: these are invented order quantities for explaining the arithmetic, not a recommended size ratio or a TONTON size chart. Assume one Rash Guard and one pair of shorts per member, using size labels already confirmed for this example.

Worked example: 24 members, two separate size listsIllustrative size label | Rash Guards | Shorts |
XS | 2 | 1 |
S | 5 | 4 |
M | 8 | 9 |
L | 6 | 7 |
XL | 3 | 3 |
Total garment units | 24 | 24 |
The order contains 24 coordinated sets and 48 garment units. Top and shorts allocations differ because the same person may wear different sizes. List spares, extra tops, colorways or sleeve variants separately; confirm how MOQ applies to each actual order configuration.

01

## Use one measuring method and one unit system
For body measurements, follow the measuring points requested for the selected pattern, with the tape level and without pulling it tight. Record the intended close or relaxed fit alongside the measurements. For a reference garment, lay it flat and identify exactly where each width or length is measured.
Ask for the measurement chart and method for the actual style before converting member measurements into order sizes. Confirm whether a waist value is relaxed, stretched, flat width or circumference. Keep centimeters and inches clearly labeled and agree the tolerance before sample approval.

02

## Check the complete kit during movement

- Try the selected Rash Guard and shorts together on the intended wearer.

- Review reaching, rotation, sitting and squatting; check opacity and seam comfort under the intended fit.

- Check the Rash Guard hem, shorts waistband and liner together for unwanted overlap or pressure.

- Record the sample size and chart version, and resolve fit changes before collecting the final size allocation.

03

## Reconcile the roster before the order is approved
Use one row per wearer or one consolidated size list, then total each garment separately. Check sleeve variants, adult or youth groups, colors and any names or numbers against the approved artwork list. Remove duplicate member entries and keep personal details out of files that do not need them.
Mark the quantities as confirmed or still being collected. If you choose spare stock, state its sizes and quantity explicitly. TONTON reviews the applicable minimums and development requirements against the complete brief.

04

## Keep a clear record for new members and reorders
Retain the approved measurement chart, fit sample, style reference and artwork version. A reorder should specify what stays the same and which quantities or sizes change. Confirm material availability, color references, MOQ and schedule again rather than assuming an earlier order automatically sets the new terms.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- This guide is not a garment measurement chart or a recommendation to order fixed percentages in each size.

- A body chest circumference cannot be compared directly with a flat garment chest width. Even doubling a flat width does not determine the correct compression fit.

- One brand’s M, L or XL does not establish the equivalent size in a different pattern.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

Should Rash Guards and shorts use the same size allocation?
Not automatically. Collect the top and shorts sizes separately because fit preferences and body proportions can differ. If you are ordering one set per member, both garment totals should match the member count, even when the size distribution differs.
Can I use another brand’s size chart?
Use it as a clearly identified reference only. Confirm the actual TONTON pattern, measuring method and sample fit before selecting order sizes; size labels are not universal.
Does this guide provide a TONTON size chart?
No. It explains measurement and quantity planning. Request the approved chart for the selected style, adult or youth fit and sample version before committing to dimensions or sizes.
How many garments are in an order for 24 matching sets?
If every set contains one Rash Guard and one pair of shorts, 24 sets contain 24 Rash Guards plus 24 pairs of shorts: 48 garment units. Extra garments and spares are counted separately.

Source basisTONTON project-brief fields and sample-review workflow. The 24-member allocation is a clearly labeled illustrative calculation; no unverified body or garment dimensions are published.Reviewed by: TONTON Product Development & Quality Control TeamLast reviewed: October 15, 2026Continue this topicCustom Rash Guard & Shorts Team Kit Buying Guide →Custom Fightwear Sampling & MOQ Guide →Custom Fightwear Quality Inspection Checklist →

Home/Resources/Custom Rash Guard & Shorts Team Kit Buying GuideCOORDINATED FIGHTWEAR KIT PROCUREMENT

# Custom Rash Guard & Shorts Team Kit Buying Guide
Plan a coordinated Rash Guard and shorts set: compare garment specifications, align artwork and colors, approve the worn kit and prepare a clear academy or private-label brief.
Reviewed October 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
A custom Rash Guard and shorts kit is two garments developed as one coordinated project. Specify the fit, fabric and construction of each garment separately, then approve shared colors, artwork placement and the worn combination together. A matching graphic does not imply matching fabric, the same size label or identical order minimums.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Define both garments and their shared identity
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Custom Rash Guard & Shorts Team Kit Buying Guide specification summaryRash Guard | Sleeve length, fit, fabric direction, opacity, seams and lower-hem requirement |
Shorts | Length, side split, shell, liner option, waistband and intended use |
Shared artwork | Logo files, color references and placement approved on each garment |
Size allocation | Separate top and shorts size quantities, linked to the same kit program |
Branding and packing | Neck branding, labels, individual names and packing requirements when included |
Approval | Review both garments together; record artwork and specification versions separately |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Academy uniform kit | A coordinated identity for members and training teams | Confirm top and shorts allocations, names and repeat-order records |
Private-label collection | A brand offering a coordinated Rash Guard and shorts range | Confirm fit, style variants, labels, packing and quantity by SKU |
High-split 2-in-1 shorts direction | Buyers comparing a high side opening with an inner layer | Inspect liner coverage, waistband comfort and the worn combination; review event requirements separately |

ORDER PLANNING

## Example brief: coordinated identity, separate specifications
This is a planning checklist, not a bundled SKU, fixed price or confirmed compatibility claim. The linked garments are reference directions; TONTON reviews the actual pairing on samples.

Example brief: coordinated identity, separate specificationsReview point | Rash Guard brief | Shorts brief |
Silhouette | Short or long sleeve; intended close fit | Leg length, side split and liner preference |
Material | Weight, composition, stretch and opacity for review | Shell and liner materials for review |
Artwork | Chest, sleeve and back placement | Leg panels, waistband and liner artwork where applicable |
Size order | Top quantity per approved size | Shorts quantity per approved size |
Worn sample | Hem control and upper-body movement | Waist security, liner coverage and leg movement |
Send a shared color reference and separate front/back artwork notes. Confirm material-specific color reproduction on physical samples, then approve the kit as a whole before bulk production.

01

## Start with the wearer and buying route
For an academy, define the members, adult or youth fit groups and whether the kit is for everyday training or a particular event. For a retail brand, define the target wearer, style count and intended collection identity. Use those requirements to choose the products rather than selecting a matching print first.

02

## Compare real product references before choosing the set
The Blue Team and White Pro Rash Guard pages provide published 220gsm product references, construction photographs and silicone lower-hem details. The High-Split 2-in-1 Grappling Shorts page shows a separate shorts construction with a high-split shell, inner layer and waistband details.
Use these pages to describe your preferred direction. Their individual evidence does not prove that a new pairing is already approved as a kit. Confirm the selected fabrics, measurements and worn combination on your project sample.

03

## Approve color and logo placement across both garments

- Use the same identified logo and artwork version for the kit.

- Specify color references and approve reproduction on each selected fabric.

- Review chest, sleeve, back and leg placements at the intended size and seam boundaries.

- Confirm how graphics meet at the waist and whether any artwork is hidden by the Rash Guard hem.

- Keep customer case photographs as production evidence; use your own permitted branding and artwork.

04

## Test the worn combination, then record the order
Review reaching, rotation and lower-body movement in the complete sample. Check the Rash Guard hem against the shorts waistband, liner coverage, skin-contact areas, opacity and seam comfort. Record changes separately for the top and shorts, then confirm the complete kit again if a change affects their interaction.
List the quantity per garment and size, labels, packing, delivery destination and target date. If each wearer receives one top and one pair of shorts, check that both garment totals agree; refer to the size and quantity guide for a worked example.

05

## Prepare the next production discussion
Send the style references, quantities, artwork status and destination through the Project Builder. TONTON reviews material options, sample requirements and the quotation scope before confirming the applicable MOQ and schedule. A coordinated kit does not imply a fixed package price or a guaranteed shared minimum across all variants.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- A shared color name or screen image is not a physical color-approval standard across different materials.

- Do not apply a verified Rash Guard fabric composition to a shorts shell or liner.

- Do not treat an academy training kit as automatically compliant with a particular competition rule set.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

Can I order custom Rash Guards and shorts as a coordinated set?
Yes. Choose Coordinated Team Kit in the Project Builder and list both garments, size quantities, artwork and construction requirements. The project review and sample approval confirm the actual pairing.
Will matching colors look identical on different fabrics?
Do not assume so from a screen reference. Review the shared color target on the selected Rash Guard, shorts shell and liner materials, and agree the physical samples used for approval.
Can one top size be paired with a different shorts size?
Record the two size choices separately in your quantity list. Confirm the measurement charts, fit and any packing requirements for mixed-size sets before approving the order.
How is the price for a custom fightwear kit confirmed?
The quote depends on each garment’s material, construction, artwork, quantities, labels and packing, along with delivery requirements. Request a project-specific quote for the complete brief rather than inferring a kit price from a product photograph.

Source basisTONTON published Blue Team and White Pro Rash Guard references, High-Split 2-in-1 Grappling Shorts product evidence, and the existing sampling and QC workflow. Page title: Rash Guard Fabric & Construction Guide | TONTON Sportswear

Home/Resources/Rash Guard Fabric & Construction GuideRASH GUARD BUYER GUIDE

# Rash Guard Fabric & Construction Guide
A buyer guide to rash guard fabric weight, composition, opacity, stretch, sublimation and silicone anti-slip hems.
Reviewed September 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
A dependable custom Rash Guard specification connects fabric weight, composition, opacity, stretch recovery, seam construction and hem control. Selected TONTON styles use 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra; the Blue Team and White Pro Club examples use 85% polyester and 15% spandex with a silicone anti-slip elastic band.

REAL PRODUCT & PROCESS EVIDENCE

## Inspect the material, construction and workflow
Original product or production photos support the specification. No generated product imagery is used.

01Stretch fabric surface and multi-row seam construction on the real sample.

02Breathable mesh inset with a clean stitched transition between panels.

03Reinforced seam intersection at a high-movement panel junction.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Rash Guard Fabric & Construction Guide specification summaryExample fabric weight | 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra |
Verified composition | 85% polyester / 15% spandex on selected styles |
Coverage direction | Opaque under stretch; reconfirmed on the approved sample |
Decoration | Sublimation-ready panel artwork |
Hem option | Silicone anti-slip elastic band |
Typical use | BJJ, MMA, grappling and team training |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
220gsm ultra-fine Lycra | Buyers prioritizing soft hand feel, strong stretch and opaque coverage | Confirm opacity, recovery and fit on the approved sample |
85% polyester / 15% spandex | Sublimated team graphics on selected verified styles | Confirm the composition belongs to the selected style |
Silicone anti-slip hem | Close-fit training where lower-hem movement needs more control | Review grip feel and placement during movement |

01

## Why fabric weight and opacity should be reviewed together
Fabric weight alone does not confirm how a garment performs when stretched. Buyers should review weight, hand feel, recovery and opacity on the same approved sample, under the intended fit direction.

02

## What the polyester-spandex blend contributes
On the verified 85/15 styles, polyester provides a smooth surface suited to sublimated graphics, while spandex provides the stretch required for a close performance fit.

03

## Construction details worth specifying

- Sleeve length and raglan panel direction

- Seam placement and stretch compatibility

- Lower-hem grip requirement

- Logo, sponsor mark and panel-artwork positions

- Size range, fit direction, private labels and packaging

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not select a fabric from GSM alone; weight does not prove opacity, recovery or comfort.

- Do not assume every TONTON Rash Guard uses the same composition or hem construction.

- Do not approve bulk production before checking the intended fit and artwork on the physical sample.

Page title: 220gsm Rash Guard Fabric: Weight, Stretch & Opacity | TONTON Sportswear

Home/Resources/220gsm Rash Guard Fabric: Weight, Stretch & OpacityRASH GUARD MATERIAL GUIDE

# 220gsm Rash Guard Fabric: Weight, Stretch & Opacity
How buyers should evaluate 220gsm Rash Guard fabric for hand feel, stretch recovery, opacity and sublimated performance wear.
Reviewed September 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
A 220gsm fabric can provide a substantial, soft and opaque Rash Guard direction, but GSM alone is not a quality guarantee. Buyers should assess fabric composition, four-way movement, recovery, opacity under the intended fit, print surface and seam compatibility on the same physical sample.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

220gsm Rash Guard Fabric: Weight, Stretch & Opacity specification summaryVerified example | 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra |
Selected composition | 85% polyester / 15% spandex on the Blue Team and White Pro styles |
Buyer priorities | Soft hand feel, elasticity, recovery and opaque coverage |
Print direction | Sublimation-compatible polyester surface on the verified 85/15 styles |
Sample test | Stretch the garment at chest, shoulder and torso fit points |
Use direction | BJJ, MMA, grappling and close-fit team training |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
220gsm direction | Programs prioritizing substantial coverage and a close performance fit | Compare hand feel, recovery and heat management on the sample |
Verified 85/15 blend | Selected styles requiring detailed sublimated graphics | Confirm the chosen SKU uses this exact composition |
Lighter fabric direction | Projects prioritizing lower weight over the verified 220gsm feel | Request a separate sample; do not infer performance from GSM alone |

01

## What 220gsm tells a buyer—and what it does not
GSM describes fabric mass per square metre. It helps compare weight directions, but it does not independently prove softness, opacity, breathability or recovery. Those qualities need to be checked together on the selected material.

02

## A practical opacity and recovery check

- Evaluate the fabric at the intended body fit

- Stretch printed and solid-color areas under consistent light

- Check whether the fabric returns smoothly after extension

- Review shoulder, chest and torso zones where strain is highest

03

## Connect material approval to the finished garment
Approve the fabric together with seam direction, sleeve construction, lower-hem control and artwork placement. This prevents an acceptable fabric swatch from becoming a poorly balanced finished Rash Guard.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not use 220gsm as a universal specification for every Rash Guard style.

- Do not call fabric opaque until it has been checked under the intended stretch and fit.

- Do not reuse the verified 85/15 composition for a product whose composition has not been confirmed.

Page title: Rash Guard Silicone Anti-Slip Band Guide | TONTON Sportswear

Home/Resources/Rash Guard Silicone Anti-Slip Band GuideRASH GUARD CONSTRUCTION GUIDE

# Rash Guard Silicone Anti-Slip Band Guide
A buyer guide to silicone anti-slip elastic bands, lower-hem control, placement and sample checks for custom Rash Guards.
Reviewed September 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
A silicone anti-slip elastic band is an interior lower-hem option designed to add grip and reduce ride-up during movement. Buyers should confirm band width, grip feel, stretch compatibility, seam finish and comfort on the worn sample rather than approving the component in isolation.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Rash Guard Silicone Anti-Slip Band Guide specification summaryComponent | Interior silicone anti-slip elastic band |
Position | Inside the lower Rash Guard hem |
Purpose | Add hem control during grappling and repeated movement |
Confirm | Width, placement, grip feel, stretch and seam comfort |
Related fit | Close performance fit |
Approval | Movement test on the physical sample |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Silicone grip band | Training where lower-hem stability is a priority | Check grip without excessive pressure or irritation |
Standard stretch hem | Projects preferring a simpler lower edge | Compare ride-up and recovery during movement |
Coordinated set | Rash Guard and shorts programs sharing visual direction | Approve each garment’s waist and hem system separately |

01

## Why lower-hem control matters
Grappling, framing and repeated torso rotation can pull a close-fit top upward. An interior grip band adds contact at the hem, helping the garment remain more stable through movement.

02

## What to put in the product brief

- Required band width and position

- Preferred grip intensity and hand feel

- Hem circumference and stretch requirement

- Seam finish at the band edge

- Intended sport and fit direction

03

## How to approve the sample
Test the hem while reaching, rotating, sprawling and returning to stance. Review stability, pressure, comfort and whether the band recovers with the surrounding fabric.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not describe a silicone band as preventing all garment movement.

- Do not choose maximum grip without considering comfort and stretch.

- Do not assume the option is included on every style.

Page title: Flatlock vs Overlock Seams for Rash Guards | TONTON Sportswear

Home/Resources/Flatlock vs Overlock Seams for Rash GuardsRASH GUARD SEAM GUIDE

# Flatlock vs Overlock Seams for Rash Guards
Compare flatlock and overlock seam directions for custom Rash Guards, including profile, stretch, comfort, reinforcement and sample approval checks.
Reviewed September 22, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Flatlock and overlock are different seam directions, not interchangeable quality labels. Flatlock can create a lower-profile seam against the body, while overlock joins cut edges efficiently and may be combined with cover stitching or reinforcement. The right choice depends on panel position, stretch, skin contact, intended use and the approved physical sample.

REAL PRODUCT & PROCESS EVIDENCE

## Inspect the material, construction and workflow
Original product or production photos support the specification. No generated product imagery is used.

01Real sample close-up showing a stretch-compatible multi-row seam.

02Panel junction where seam profile, reinforcement and stretch must work together.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Flatlock vs Overlock Seams for Rash Guards specification summaryFlatlock direction | Lower-profile seam with thread visible across the joined edges |
Overlock direction | Joined cut edges; may be paired with cover stitching or topstitching |
Primary checks | Profile, stretch, recovery, abrasion and seam comfort |
High-movement zones | Shoulders, underarms, side panels and torso junctions |
Approval method | Inside and outside inspection plus worn movement test |
Final control | Record seam type and position in the approved specification |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Flatlock direction | Close-fit panels where a lower seam profile is preferred | Check stretch, thread coverage and comfort against skin |
Overlock + cover direction | Efficient panel joining with a controlled outer finish | Confirm bulk, recovery and the exact cover-stitch route |
Reinforced junction | High-load panel intersections and repeated movement zones | Inspect backtacking, thread tension and stretch compatibility |

01

## Understand the construction before naming it
A finished seam can look similar from the outside while using a different joining method underneath. Buyers should review both sides of the garment and record the actual stitch direction used at each panel.

02

## Match seam direction to the body zone

- Use a low-profile direction where the garment stays close to skin

- Review underarm and shoulder stretch through full reach

- Reinforce panel junctions without creating a hard contact point

- Keep thread and stitch density compatible with fabric recovery

03

## Approve the complete seam system
Inspect skipped stitches, waviness, exposed cut edges, thread tension and recovery. Then wear-test reaching, rotation and grappling movement before bulk approval.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not call every visible multi-row seam flatlock without checking the reverse construction.

- Do not select a seam only by appearance; thread, fabric and panel direction affect performance.

- Do not approve seam comfort from a flat sample without a worn movement test.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

Is flatlock always better for a Rash Guard?
No. Flatlock can offer a low-profile direction, but the best construction depends on the panel, fabric, thread, intended fit and approved sample.
Can overlock be used on stretch performance fabric?
Yes. It can join stretch panels effectively when stitch balance, thread and reinforcement are specified for the material and use.
How should buyers confirm a seam type?
Review the inside and outside construction, identify the stitch route in the specification and approve it through a worn movement test.

# High-Split vs Standard-Split Grappling Shorts
Compare high-split and standard-split grappling shorts for kicking clearance, coverage, silhouette and combat-sport movement.
Reviewed September 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Choose split height from the athlete’s movement and coverage requirements. An ultra-high split maximizes thigh clearance for kicks, shots, sprawls and wide positions; a standard split creates a more conventional outer silhouette. A fitted inner liner can preserve support and coverage beneath a high-split shell.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

High-Split vs Standard-Split Grappling Shorts specification summaryHigh-split direction | Maximum leg clearance and gladiator-style silhouette |
Standard-split direction | More conventional outer coverage |
Coverage system | Review outer opening together with the inner liner |
Movement test | High kick, shot, sprawl and wide stance |
Fit control | Waist stability and shell recovery |
Approval | Sport-specific worn sample |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Ultra-high split | MMA, grappling and movement-led training | Confirm opening height and liner coverage |
Standard split | Buyers preferring a more conventional outer short | Check whether the shell restricts the target range |
No liner direction | Projects requiring a separate base layer | Clarify coverage, seam and waistband requirements |

01

## Start with the required range of motion
High kicks, guard entries, shots and wide grappling positions place different demands on the thigh opening. The selected cut should release the leg without making the waistband or remaining shell carry unnecessary tension.

02

## Balance mobility and coverage
A deep outer split increases clearance. In a 2-in-1 construction, the fitted liner becomes the coverage layer and should be checked for length, opacity, support and seam comfort.

03

## Record the approval points

- Split height and curve

- Outer-short length

- Liner length and fit

- Waistband position

- Movement result from front, side and rear views

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not select split height from appearance alone.

- Do not evaluate outer coverage without the intended inner layer.

- Do not assume one split shape fits every sport or target customer.

A 2-in-1 grappling short combines a mobile outer shell with a fitted compression liner. The current TONTON high-split sample uses a breathable quick-dry four-way stretch shell and a soft 250gsm milk-silk liner; buyers should confirm liner length, opacity, support, seam comfort and artwork stretch on the physical sample.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

# Training Shorts Fabric, Ventilation & Pocket Guide
A buyer guide to lightweight stretch woven fabric, perforated ventilation, zip pockets, adjustable waistbands and reinforced construction for functional training shorts.
Reviewed September 22, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Functional training shorts should balance movement, airflow, secure storage and waist stability. A practical specification starts with lightweight stretch woven fabric, then defines perforated ventilation, zip-pocket construction, waistband adjustment, crotch mobility and reinforced stitching for the intended gym, HIIT, combat-training or outdoor use.

REAL PRODUCT & PROCESS EVIDENCE

## Inspect the material, construction and workflow
Original product or production photos support the specification. No generated product imagery is used.

01Real sample detail showing perforated ventilation beside a secure zip pocket.

02Adjustable waistband area with reinforced topstitching.

03Interior adjustment and branding details that should be confirmed on the sample.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Training Shorts Fabric, Ventilation & Pocket Guide specification summaryFabric direction | Lightweight polyester- or nylon-based stretch woven performance fabric |
Movement | Confirm lateral and recovery stretch for squats, lunges and kicks |
Ventilation | Perforated side detail; hole method and edge stability require confirmation |
Storage | Secure side zip pocket for small items |
Waist control | Elastic and adjustable construction; confirm drawcord or tab route |
Use direction | Gym, HIIT, functional fitness, combat training and outdoor activity |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Polyester stretch woven | Quick-dry training programs and custom color directions | Confirm composition, weight, recovery and abrasion performance |
Nylon stretch woven | Buyers prioritizing a smooth hand feel and abrasion direction | Confirm actual composition and colorfastness before claiming performance |
Perforation + zip pocket | Multi-use training shorts needing airflow and secure storage | Check hole-edge stability, pocket bag, zipper and skin contact |

01

## Start with movement and recovery
The shell should release the hips and thighs during squats, lunges, jumps and kicking drills, then recover without bagging. Confirm stretch direction and finished-garment mobility together.

02

## Specify ventilation and storage as constructions

- Define perforation position, spacing and edge quality

- Confirm zipper type, opening length and puller direction

- Inspect pocket-bag depth and attachment

- Check whether internal components rub during movement

- Record reinforcement at the pocket ends and high-load seams

03

## Approve the intended use honestly
This direction suits gym, HIIT, cross-training, combat conditioning and light outdoor use. Competition eligibility and water resistance require separate evidence and should not be inferred from appearance.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not call a zip pocket waterproof unless its zipper, seam and pocket construction have been verified.

- Do not publish a fabric composition or GSM until it belongs to the selected approved style.

- Do not assume a utility training short automatically meets combat-sport competition rules.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

What fabric is suitable for functional training shorts?
A lightweight stretch woven polyester or nylon direction is common, but composition, GSM, stretch and recovery should be confirmed on the selected sample.
Are perforated holes the same as mesh panels?
No. Perforation creates openings in a panel, while mesh is a separate open-structure material. Each requires different edge and seam checks.
Can these shorts be used for MMA training?
They can suit conditioning, bag work and general combat training, but formal competition or grappling use should be confirmed against equipment rules and real wear testing.

# Custom Fightwear Quality Inspection Checklist
A practical QC checklist for custom Rash Guards and fight shorts covering material, print, measurements, seams, waist systems, labels and packing.
Reviewed September 22, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
A useful fightwear inspection compares the finished order with the approved sample and specification. Check material identity, color and print placement, measurements, stretch seams, waist and closure systems, labels, workmanship and packing using recorded tolerances and an agreed sampling plan.

REAL PRODUCT & PROCESS EVIDENCE

## Inspect the material, construction and workflow
Original product or production photos support the specification. No generated product imagery is used.

01Stitching, construction and measurement checks against the approved specification.

02Finished-garment review before packing and order handover.

03Packing review after final product checks are completed.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Custom Fightwear Quality Inspection Checklist specification summaryReference | Approved sample, artwork and product specification |
Material | Composition/weight where confirmed, hand feel, color and stretch direction |
Construction | Seams, reinforcement, waistband, closure, liner and hems |
Branding | Artwork scale, placement, color direction, labels and logo finish |
Measurements | Agreed points of measure and tolerances across requested sizes |
Packing | Labels, folding, bagging, quantity and carton requirements |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Pre-production approval | New products, fits, materials and artwork | Freeze the sample and specification before bulk work |
In-line inspection | Orders needing process checks before completion | Confirm checkpoints, quantity stage and issue escalation |
Final inspection | Finished orders before packing or shipment | Use the agreed sampling plan, tolerances and packing brief |

01

## Freeze the inspection reference
Before inspection begins, identify the approved sample, artwork version, size specification, labels, packaging and any accepted revisions. A checklist without a controlled reference cannot prove conformity.

02

## Inspect product-specific risk points

- Rash Guard opacity, recovery, stretch seams and lower-hem control

- Fight-short waistband, drawstring, hook-and-loop closure and split reinforcement

- 2-in-1 liner length, opacity, seam comfort and attachment

- Print alignment, logo position and visible color variation

- Skipped stitches, open seams, puckering and loose thread

03

## Record issues for corrective action
Record the affected style, size, defect location, quantity and severity. Recheck corrected goods against the same approved reference before packing or shipment.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- A checklist does not replace product-specific tolerances and an approved sample.

- Do not claim a laboratory result without a corresponding test report.

- Do not accept appearance-only inspection where size, stretch, closure or seam function matters.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

What should be used as the main QC reference?
Use the approved sample together with the latest artwork, measurement specification, construction notes, labels and packing requirements.
Is final inspection enough for a new product?
Not always. New materials, prints or constructions may benefit from pre-production and in-line checks so issues are found before the order is complete.
Should every product use the same checklist?
The inspection framework can be shared, but risk points and tolerances must be adjusted for each product and approved specification.

# How to Prepare Artwork for Sublimation
Prepare logos, colors, panel artwork and approval notes for custom sublimated Rash Guards, fight shorts and teamwear.
Reviewed September 22, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Prepare sublimation artwork by supplying vector logos where available, naming brand colors, separating priority and secondary marks, identifying placement by garment panel and noting any alignment requirement across seams. Final production artwork should be confirmed on the supplier template and approved through a mockup and physical sample.

REAL PRODUCT & PROCESS EVIDENCE

## Inspect the material, construction and workflow
Original product or production photos support the specification. No generated product imagery is used.

01Artwork and layout preparation before the production file is finalized.

02Product, logo, color and construction requirements are confirmed as one brief.

03Approved artwork moves into the sublimation printing stage before cutting and sewing.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

How to Prepare Artwork for Sublimation specification summaryPreferred logo input | Vector AI, EPS, SVG or editable PDF where available |
Raster references | Supply the highest available resolution at intended use size |
Color direction | Provide Pantone or brand references when color matching matters |
Placement map | Identify front, back, sleeve, side and waistband positions |
Panel control | Confirm bleed, seam crossings, alignment and safe zones on the supplier template |
Approval route | Mockup review followed by physical sample confirmation |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Vector logo | Scalable sponsor and brand marks | Check outlines, transparency and the approved color reference |
High-resolution raster art | Textures and photographic-style graphics | Confirm resolution at production size and panel bleed |
Panel-to-panel artwork | Designs that visually continue across seams | Set alignment expectations and review size grading on the mockup |

01

## Send an organized artwork package

- Separate logos from visual references

- Name each mark and intended position

- Identify mandatory brand colors

- List priority, secondary and optional artwork

- Provide editable files and font information where permitted

02

## Design around garment panels
Sublimation is applied to panels before the garment is sewn. Important text, faces, small sponsor marks and alignment features need safe space from seam allowances and high-stretch zones.

03

## Approve both mockup and physical result
The mockup controls layout and hierarchy. The sample confirms printed color direction, scale, seam interaction and how artwork appears on the worn garment. Record every accepted revision before bulk production.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not assume a low-resolution screenshot can be enlarged cleanly for production.

- Do not treat screen color as proof of printed color; confirm the physical sample.

- Do not place critical text or small marks on seam allowances or high-distortion zones.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

Do I need final artwork before requesting a quote?
No. A product direction, logos and references can start the discussion, but production-ready artwork is required before print approval.
Which logo format is best for sublimation?
Vector AI, EPS, SVG or editable PDF is preferred because it can scale cleanly. High-resolution raster files may work for suitable graphics.
Why can printed color differ from a monitor?
Screens emit light while fabric printing depends on ink, material, heat and viewing conditions. Approve critical colors on a physical sample.

# Custom Fightwear Sampling & MOQ Guide
A practical guide to preparing artwork, specifications, samples and quantity information for a custom fightwear project.
Reviewed September 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Start with the product type, estimated quantity, intended use, size range, artwork status and destination market. The applicable MOQ, sample route and production timing are confirmed after the selected product, material and construction requirements are reviewed.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Custom Fightwear Sampling & MOQ Guide specification summaryStarting information | Product, quantity, use, sizes, artwork and destination |
MOQ | Confirmed for the selected product, quantity and specification |
Mockup | Artwork, color and logo placement review |
Sample review | Fit, material, construction, branding and workmanship |
Bulk approval | Begins against the approved sample and specification |
Schedule | Confirmed for the specific project after review |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Digital mockup first | Projects still resolving artwork, color and logo placement | Provide vector logos and visual references where available |
Physical sample review | New fits, materials, construction or private-label programs | Record the approved fit, color, material, seams and branding |
Repeat specification | Reorders based on an already approved product | Identify the previous specification and list every requested change |

01

## What to prepare before requesting a quote

- Product type and estimated quantity

- Target users and intended sport

- Required sizes and fit direction

- Vector logo or available artwork

- Reference product and construction priorities

- Destination country and preferred contact method

02

## Why MOQ and timing are project-specific
Materials, printing method, construction, size assortment, artwork readiness and packaging can change the production route. A supplier should confirm the schedule and applicable MOQ against the actual brief instead of treating one number as universal.

03

## What the approved sample controls
The approved sample is the practical reference for fit, color direction, material, artwork placement, seam construction, labels and other confirmed details before bulk work begins.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not treat one MOQ as universal across different products, materials and specifications.

- A digital mockup cannot replace physical checks for fit, hand feel, opacity or construction.

- Do not set a production schedule before material, artwork, quantity and packaging are reviewed.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

Is one MOQ used for every custom fightwear product?
No. The applicable MOQ depends on the selected product, material, construction, artwork, quantity mix and project requirements.
Can a digital mockup replace a physical sample?
A mockup helps approve layout, but it cannot confirm fit, hand feel, opacity, stretch, seam comfort or finished workmanship.
What information is needed to start?
Provide the product type, estimated quantity, intended use, sizes, artwork status, destination and any construction priorities.
